segs.p: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.1
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.1

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Sambodhisutta
segs.e: Awakening

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “Sace, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, if wanderers of other religions were to ask:

segs.p: ‘sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ kā upanisā bhāvanāyā’ti, evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ kinti byākareyyāthā”ti?
segs.e: ‘Reverends, what is the vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening?’ How would you answer them?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā …pe… bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. … The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Sace, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, if wanderers of other religions were to ask:

segs.p: ‘sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ kā upanisā bhāvanāyā’ti, evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: ‘Reverends, what is the vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening?’ You should answer them:

segs.p: ‘Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ ayaṁ paṭhamā upanisā bhāvanāya.
segs.e: This is the first vital condition for the development of the awakening factors.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ ayaṁ dutiyā upanisā bhāvanāya.
segs.e: This is the second vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāyaṁ kathā abhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṁsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant gets to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is, talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ ayaṁ tatiyā upanisā bhāvanāya.
segs.e: This is the third vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: Sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ ayaṁ catutthī upanisā bhāvanāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: Sambodhipakkhikānaṁ, āvuso, dhammānaṁ ayaṁ pañcamī upanisā bhāvanāya’.
segs.e: This is the fifth vital condition for the development of the qualities on the same side as awakening.’

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa—
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: sīlavā bhavissati, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharissati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhissati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: be ethical …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa—
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: yāyaṁ kathā abhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṁsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī bhavissati akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa—
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharissati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: live with energy roused up …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa—
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: paññavā bhavissati udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: be wise …

segs.p: Tena ca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā imesu pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya cattāro dhammā uttari bhāvetabbā—
segs.e: But then, a mendicant grounded on these five things should develop four further things.

segs.p: asubhā bhāvetabbā rāgassa pahānāya, mettā bhāvetabbā byāpādassa pahānāya, ānāpānassati bhāvetabbā vitakkupacchedāya, aniccasaññā bhāvetabbā asmimānasamugghātāya.
segs.e: They should develop the perception of ugliness to give up greed, love to give up hate, mindfulness of breathing to cut off thinking, and perception of impermanence to uproot the conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Aniccasaññino, bhikkhave, anattasaññā saṇṭhāti.
segs.e: When you perceive impermanence, the perception of not-self becomes stabilized.

segs.p: Anattasaññī asmimānasamugghātaṁ pāpuṇāti diṭṭheva dhamme nibbānan”ti.
segs.e: Perceiving not-self, you uproot the conceit ‘I am’ and attain extinguishment in this very life.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.2
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.2

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Nissayasutta
segs.e: Supported

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “‘nissayasampanno nissayasampanno’ti, bhante, vuccati.
segs.e: “Sir, they speak of being ‘supported’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu nissayasampanno hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a mendicant who is supported defined?”

segs.p: “Saddhañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya akusalaṁ pajahati kusalaṁ bhāveti, pahīnamevassa taṁ akusalaṁ hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicant, if a mendicant supported by faith gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful, the unskillful is actually given up by them.

segs.p: Hiriñce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant supported by conscience …

segs.p: ottappañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant supported by prudence …

segs.p: vīriyañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant supported by energy …

segs.p: paññañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya akusalaṁ pajahati kusalaṁ bhāveti, pahīnamevassa taṁ akusalaṁ hoti.
segs.e: If a mendicant supported by wisdom gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful, the unskillful is actually given up by them.

segs.p: Taṁ hissa bhikkhuno akusalaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti suppahīnaṁ, yaṁsa ariyāya paññāya disvā pahīnaṁ.
segs.e: What’s been given up is completely given up when it has been given up by seeing with noble wisdom.

segs.p: Tena ca pana, bhikkhu, bhikkhunā imesu pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya cattāro upanissāya vihātabbā.
segs.e: But then, a mendicant grounded on these five things should rely on four things.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṁ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṁ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṁ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṁ vinodeti.
segs.e: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and dispels some things.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissayasampanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is supported.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.3
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.3

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Meghiyasutta
segs.e: With Meghiya

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā cālikāyaṁ viharati cālikāpabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Cālikā, on the Cālikā mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā meghiyo bhagavato upaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time Venerable Meghiya was the Buddha’s attendant.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā meghiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho āyasmā meghiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Meghiya went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “icchāmahaṁ, bhante, jantugāmaṁ piṇḍāya pavisitun”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’d like to enter Jantu village for alms.”

segs.p: “Yassadāni tvaṁ, meghiya, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.
segs.e: “Please, Meghiya, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā meghiyo pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya jantugāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then Meghiya robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Jantu village for alms.

segs.p: Jantugāme piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena kimikāḷāya nadiyā tīraṁ tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: After the meal, on his return from almsround in Jantu village, he went to the shore of Kimikālā River.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā meghiyo kimikāḷāya nadiyā tīre jaṅghāvihāraṁ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno ambavanaṁ pāsādikaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: As he was going for a walk along the shore of the river he saw a lovely and delightful mango grove.

segs.p: Disvānassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Seeing this, it occurred to him,

segs.p: “pāsādikaṁ vatidaṁ ambavanaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ, alaṁ vatidaṁ kulaputtassa padhānatthikassa padhānāya.
segs.e: “Oh, this mango grove is lovely and delightful! This is good enough for striving for a gentleman wanting to strive.

segs.p: Sace maṁ bhagavā anujāneyya, āgaccheyyāhaṁ imaṁ ambavanaṁ padhānāyā”ti.
segs.e: If the Buddha allows me, I’ll come back to this mango grove to meditate.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā meghiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā meghiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Meghiya went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding,

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya jantugāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ.
Jantugāme piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena kimikāḷāya nadiyā tīraṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁ.
Addasaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, kimikāḷāya nadiyā tīre jaṅghāvihāraṁ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno ambavanaṁ pāsādikaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ.
Disvāna me etadahosi:
‘pāsādikaṁ vatidaṁ ambavanaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ.
Alaṁ vatidaṁ kulaputtassa padhānatthikassa padhānāya.
Sace maṁ bhagavā anujāneyya, āgaccheyyāhaṁ imaṁ ambavanaṁ padhānāyā’ti.
Sace maṁ bhagavā anujāneyya, gaccheyyāhaṁ taṁ ambavanaṁ padhānāyā”ti.
segs.e: “If the Buddha allows me, I’ll go back to that mango grove to meditate.”

segs.p: “Āgamehi tāva, meghiya. Ekakamhi tāva yāva aññopi koci bhikkhu āgacchatī”ti.
segs.e: “We’re alone, Meghiya. Wait until another mendicant comes.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā meghiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time Meghiya said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “bhagavato, bhante, natthi kiñci uttari karaṇīyaṁ, natthi katassa paṭicayo.
segs.e: “Sir, the Buddha has nothing more to do, and nothing that needs improvement.

segs.p: Mayhaṁ kho pana, bhante, atthi uttari karaṇīyaṁ, atthi katassa paṭicayo.
segs.e: But I have.

segs.p: Sace maṁ bhagavā anujāneyya, gaccheyyāhaṁ taṁ ambavanaṁ padhānāyā”ti.
segs.e: If you allow me, I’ll go back to that mango grove to meditate.”

segs.p: “Āgamehi tāva, meghiya, ekakamhi tāva yāva aññopi koci bhikkhu āgacchatī”ti.
segs.e: “We’re alone, Meghiya. Wait until another mendicant comes.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā meghiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time Meghiya said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “bhagavato, bhante, natthi kiñci uttari karaṇīyaṁ, natthi katassa paṭicayo.
segs.e: “Sir, the Buddha has nothing more to do, and nothing that needs improvement.

segs.p: Mayhaṁ kho pana, bhante, atthi uttari karaṇīyaṁ, atthi katassa paṭicayo.
segs.e: But I have.

segs.p: Sace maṁ bhagavā anujāneyya, gaccheyyāhaṁ taṁ ambavanaṁ padhānāyā”ti.
segs.e: If you allow me, I’ll go back to that mango grove to meditate.”

segs.p: “Padhānanti kho, meghiya, vadamānaṁ kinti vadeyyāma.
segs.e: “Meghiya, since you speak of striving in meditation, what can I say?

segs.p: Yassadāni tvaṁ, meghiya, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.
segs.e: Please, Meghiya, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā meghiyo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yena taṁ ambavanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ ambavanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Meghiya got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he went to that mango grove, and, having plunged deep into it, sat at the root of a certain tree for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato meghiyassa tasmiṁ ambavane viharantassa yebhuyyena tayo pāpakā akusalā vitakkā samudācaranti, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: But while Meghiya was meditating in that mango grove he was beset mostly by three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts, namely,

segs.p: kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṁsāvitakko.
segs.e: sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato meghiyassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then he thought,

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho.
segs.e: “Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!

segs.p: Saddhāya ca vatamhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā;
segs.e: I’ve gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness,

segs.p: atha ca panimehi tīhi pāpakehi akusalehi vitakkehi anvāsattā—
segs.e: but I’m still harassed by these three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts:

segs.p: kāmavitakkena, byāpādavitakkena, vihiṁsāvitakkenā”ti.
segs.e: sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā meghiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā meghiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Meghiya went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, tasmiṁ ambavane viharantassa yebhuyyena tayo pāpakā akusalā vitakkā samudācaranti, seyyathidaṁ—
kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṁsāvitakko.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi:
‘acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho.
Saddhāya ca vatamhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā;
atha ca panimehi tīhi pāpakehi akusalehi vitakkehi anvāsattā—
kāmavitakkena, byāpādavitakkena, vihiṁsāvitakkenā’”ti.
“Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā pañca dhammā paripakkāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Meghiya, when the heart’s release is not ripe, five things help it ripen.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, meghiya, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā ayaṁ paṭhamo dhammo paripakkāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā ayaṁ dutiyo dhammo paripakkāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, meghiya, yāyaṁ kathā abhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṁsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant gets to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is, talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā ayaṁ tatiyo dhammo paripakkāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā ayaṁ catuttho dhammo paripakkāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: Aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā ayaṁ pañcamo dhammo paripakkāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that, when the heart’s release is not ripe, helps it ripen.

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa:
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: ‘sīlavā bhavissati …pe… samādāya sikkhissati sikkhāpadesu’.
segs.e: be ethical …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa:
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to

segs.p: ‘yāyaṁ kathā abhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—appicchakathā …pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī bhavissati akicchalābhī akasiralābhī’.
segs.e: take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa: ‘āraddhavīriyo viharissati …pe… anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu’.
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to be energetic …

segs.p: Kalyāṇamittassetaṁ, meghiya, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṁ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa: ‘paññavā bhavissati …pe… sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā’.
segs.e: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to be wise …

segs.p: Tena ca pana, meghiya, bhikkhunā imesu pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya cattāro dhammā uttari bhāvetabbā—
segs.e: But then, a mendicant grounded on these five things should develop four further things.

segs.p: asubhā bhāvetabbā rāgassa pahānāya, mettā bhāvetabbā byāpādassa pahānāya, ānāpānassati bhāvetabbā vitakkupacchedāya, aniccasaññā bhāvetabbā asmimānasamugghātāya.
segs.e: They should develop the perception of ugliness to give up greed, love to give up hate, mindfulness of breathing to cut off thinking, and perception of impermanence to uproot the conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Aniccasaññino, meghiya, anattasaññā saṇṭhāti.
segs.e: When you perceive impermanence, the perception of not-self becomes stabilized.

segs.p: Anattasaññī asmimānasamugghātaṁ pāpuṇāti diṭṭheva dhamme nibbānan”ti.
segs.e: Perceiving not-self, you uproot the conceit ‘I am’ and attain extinguishment in this very life.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.4
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.4

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Nandakasutta
segs.e: With Nandaka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nandako upaṭṭhānasālāyaṁ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Nandaka was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants in the assembly hall with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bahidvārakoṭṭhake aṭṭhāsi kathāpariyosānaṁ āgamayamāno.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the assembly hall. He stood outside the door waiting for the talk to end.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā kathāpariyosānaṁ viditvā ukkāsetvā aggaḷaṁ ākoṭesi.
segs.e: When he knew the talk had ended he cleared his throat and knocked on the door-panel.

segs.p: Vivariṁsu kho te bhikkhū bhagavato dvāraṁ.
segs.e: The mendicants opened the door for the Buddha,

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā upaṭṭhānasālaṁ pavisitvā paññattāsane nisīdi.
segs.e: and he entered the assembly hall, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nandakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He said to Nandaka,

segs.p: “dīgho kho tyāyaṁ, nandaka, dhammapariyāyo bhikkhūnaṁ paṭibhāsi.
segs.e: “Nandaka, that was a long exposition of the teaching you gave to the mendicants.

segs.p: Api me piṭṭhi āgilāyati bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitassa kathāpariyosānaṁ āgamayamānassā”ti.
segs.e: My back was aching while I stood outside the door waiting for the talk to end.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā nandako sārajjamānarūpo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Nandaka felt embarrassed and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “na kho pana mayaṁ, bhante, jānāma ‘bhagavā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito’ti.
segs.e: “Sir, we didn’t know that the Buddha was standing outside the door.

segs.p: Sace hi mayaṁ, bhante, jāneyyāma ‘bhagavā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito’ti, ettakampi (…) no nappaṭibhāseyyā”ti.
segs.e: If we’d known, I wouldn’t have said so much.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nandakaṁ sārajjamānarūpaṁ viditvā āyasmantaṁ nandakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that Nandaka was embarrassed, said to him,

segs.p: “sādhu sādhu, nandaka.
segs.e: “Good, good, Nandaka!

segs.p: Etaṁ kho, nandaka, tumhākaṁ patirūpaṁ kulaputtānaṁ saddhāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitānaṁ, yaṁ tumhe dhammiyā kathāya sannisīdeyyātha.
segs.e: It’s appropriate for gentlemen like you, who have gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, to sit together for a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Sannipatitānaṁ vo, nandaka, dvayaṁ karaṇīyaṁ—
segs.e: When you’re sitting together you should do one of two things:

segs.p: dhammī vā kathā ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo.
segs.e: discuss the teachings or keep noble silence.

segs.p: Saddho ca, nandaka, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā.
segs.e: Nandaka, a mendicant is faithful but not ethical.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect,

segs.p: Tena taṁ aṅgaṁ paripūretabbaṁ:
segs.e: and should fulfill it, thinking,

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ sīlavā cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can I become faithful and ethical?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.
segs.e: When a mendicant is faithful and ethical, they’re complete in that respect.

segs.p: Saddho ca, nandaka, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca, no ca lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa.
segs.e: A mendicant is faithful and ethical, but does not get internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect,

segs.p: Tena taṁ aṅgaṁ paripūretabbaṁ:
segs.e: and should fulfill it, thinking,

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissā’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can I become faithful and ethical and get internal serenity of heart?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.
segs.e: When a mendicant is faithful and ethical and gets internal serenity of heart, they’re complete in that respect.

segs.p: Saddho ca, nandaka, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: A mendicant is faithful, ethical, and gets internal serenity of heart, but they don’t get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, nandaka, pāṇako catuppādako assa.
segs.e: Suppose, Nandaka, there was a four-footed animal

segs.p: Tassa eko pādo omako lāmako.
segs.e: that was lame and disabled.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro assa.
segs.e: It would be incomplete in that respect.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant is faithful, ethical, and gets internal serenity of heart, but they don’t get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect,

segs.p: Tena taṁ aṅgaṁ paripūretabbaṁ:
segs.e: and should fulfill it, thinking,

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can I become faithful and ethical and get internal serenity of heart and get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hotī”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant is faithful and ethical and gets internal serenity of heart and gets the higher wisdom of discernment of principles, they’re complete in that respect.”

segs.p: Idamavoca bhagavā.
segs.e: That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nandako acirapakkantassa bhagavato bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, not long after the Buddha left, Venerable Nandaka said to the mendicants,

segs.p: “idāni, āvuso, bhagavā catūhi padehi kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “Just now, reverends, the Buddha revealed a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure in four statements, before getting up from his seat and entering his dwelling:

segs.p: ‘saddho ca, nandaka, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā.
segs.e: ‘Nandaka, a mendicant is faithful but not ethical.

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect,

segs.p: Tena taṁ aṅgaṁ paripūretabbaṁ—
segs.e: and should fulfill it, thinking,

segs.p: kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ sīlavā cā’ti.
segs.e: “How can I become faithful and ethical?”

segs.p: Yato ca kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.
segs.e: When a mendicant is faithful and ethical, they’re complete in that respect.

segs.p: Saddho ca, nandaka, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca, no ca lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa …pe…
segs.e: A mendicant is faithful and ethical, but does not get internal serenity of heart. …

segs.p: lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya,
segs.e: They get internal serenity of heart, but they don’t get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti.
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, nandaka, pāṇako catuppādako assa, tassa eko pādo omako lāmako,
segs.e: Suppose, Nandaka, there was a four-footed animal that was lame and disabled.

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro assa.
segs.e: It would be incomplete in that respect.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca, lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya,
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant is faithful, ethical, and gets internal serenity of heart, but they don’t get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti,
segs.e: So they’re incomplete in that respect,

segs.p: tena taṁ aṅgaṁ paripūretabbaṁ
segs.e: and should fulfill it, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ sīlavā ca, lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa, lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti.
segs.e: “How can I become faithful and ethical and get internal serenity of heart and get the higher wisdom of discernment of principles?”

segs.p: Yato ca kho, nandaka, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamādhissa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya,
segs.e: When a mendicant is faithful and ethical and gets internal serenity of heart and gets the higher wisdom of discernment of principles,

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hotīti.
segs.e: they’re complete in that respect.’

segs.p: Pañcime, āvuso, ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: Reverends, there are these five benefits of listening to the teachings at the right time and discussing the teachings at the right time.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant teaches Dhamma to the mendicants that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti tathā tathā so satthu piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: Whenever they do this, they become liked and approved by the Teacher, respected and admired.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, āvuso, paṭhamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: This is the first benefit …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti. Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches the mendicants the Dhamma …

segs.p: brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: Whenever they do this, they feel inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, āvuso, dutiyo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: This is the second benefit …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches the mendicants the Dhamma …

segs.p: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe… brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme gambhīraṁ atthapadaṁ paññāya ativijjha passati.
segs.e: Whenever they do this, they see the meaning of a deep saying in that Dhamma with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, āvuso, tatiyo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: This is the third benefit …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe… brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches the mendicants the Dhamma …

segs.p: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe… brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti tathā tathā naṁ sabrahmacārī uttari sambhāventi:
segs.e: Whenever they do this, their spiritual companions esteem them more highly, thinking,

segs.p: ‘addhā ayamāyasmā patto vā pajjati vā’.
segs.e: ‘For sure this venerable has attained or will attain.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ, āvuso, catuttho ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth benefit …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches the mendicants the Dhamma …

segs.p: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti, tattha ye kho bhikkhū sekhā appattamānasā anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ patthayamānā viharanti, te taṁ dhammaṁ sutvā vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: Whenever they do this, there may be trainee mendicants present, who haven’t achieved their heart’s desire, but live aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke. Hearing that teaching, they rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

segs.p: Ye pana tattha bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojanā sammadaññāvimuttā, te taṁ dhammaṁ sutvā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṁyeva anuyuttā viharanti.
segs.e: There may be perfected mendicants present, who have ended the defilements, completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and are rightly freed through enlightenment. Hearing that teaching, they simply live happily in this life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, āvuso, pañcamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāya.
segs.e: This is the fifth benefit …

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, pañca ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena dhammasākacchāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of listening to the teachings at the right time and discussing the teachings at the right time.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.5
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.5

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Balasutta
segs.e: Powers

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, balāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these four powers.

segs.p: Katamāni cattāri?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Paññābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, anavajjabalaṁ, saṅgāhabalaṁ.
segs.e: The powers of wisdom, energy, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.

segs.p: Katamañca, bhikkhave, paññābalaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the power of wisdom?

segs.p: Ye dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā ye dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sāvajjā sāvajjasaṅkhātā ye dhammā anavajjā anavajjasaṅkhātā ye dhammā kaṇhā kaṇhasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sukkā sukkasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā ye dhammā asevitabbā asevitabbasaṅkhātā ye dhammā nālamariyā nālamariyasaṅkhātā ye dhammā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā, tyassa dhammā paññāya vodiṭṭhā honti vocaritā.
segs.e: One has clearly seen and clearly contemplated with wisdom those qualities that are skillful and considered to be skillful; those that are unskillful … blameworthy … blameless … dark … bright … to be cultivated … not to be cultivated … not worthy of the noble ones … worthy of the noble ones and considered to be worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, paññābalaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the power of wisdom.

segs.p: Katamañca, bhikkhave, vīriyabalaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the power of energy?

segs.p: Ye dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sāvajjā sāvajjasaṅkhātā ye dhammā kaṇhā kaṇhasaṅkhātā ye dhammā asevitabbā asevitabbasaṅkhātā ye dhammā nālamariyā nālamariyasaṅkhātā, tesaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: One generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives to give up those qualities that are unskillful and considered to be unskillful; those that are blameworthy … dark … not to be cultivated … not worthy of the noble ones and considered to be not worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Ye dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā ye dhammā anavajjā anavajjasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sukkā sukkasaṅkhātā ye dhammā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā ye dhammā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā, tesaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: One generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives to gain those qualities that are skillful and considered to be skillful; those that are blameless … bright … to be cultivated … worthy of the noble ones and considered to be worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, vīriyabalaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the power of energy.

segs.p: Katamañca, bhikkhave, anavajjabalaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the power of blamelessness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako anavajjena kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena manokammena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has blameless conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, anavajjabalaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the power of blamelessness.

segs.p: Katamañca, bhikkhave, saṅgāhabalaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the power of inclusiveness?

segs.p: Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, saṅgahavatthūni—
segs.e: There are these four ways of being inclusive.

segs.p: dānaṁ, peyyavajjaṁ, atthacariyā, samānattatā.
segs.e: Giving, kindly words, taking care, and equality.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, dānānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammadānaṁ.
segs.e: The best of gifts is the gift of the teaching.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, peyyavajjānaṁ yadidaṁ atthikassa ohitasotassa punappunaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: The best sort of kindly speech is to teach the Dhamma again and again to someone who is engaged and who actively listens.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, atthacariyānaṁ yadidaṁ assaddhaṁ saddhāsampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti, dussīlaṁ sīlasampadāya … macchariṁ cāgasampadāya … duppaññaṁ paññāsampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: The best way of taking care is to encourage, settle, and ground the unfaithful in faith, the unethical in ethics, the stingy in generosity, and the ignorant in wisdom.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, samānattatānaṁ yadidaṁ sotāpanno sotāpannassa samānatto, sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmissa samānatto, anāgāmī anāgāmissa samānatto, arahā arahato samānatto.
segs.e: The best kind of equality is the equality of a stream-enterer with another stream-enterer, a once-returner with another once-returner, a non-returner with another non-returner, and a perfected one with another perfected one.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, saṅgāhabalaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the power of inclusiveness.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri balāni.
segs.e: These are the four powers.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi balehi samannāgato ariyasāvako pañca bhayāni samatikkanto hoti.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four powers has got past five fears.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Ājīvikabhayaṁ, asilokabhayaṁ, parisasārajjabhayaṁ, maraṇabhayaṁ, duggatibhayaṁ.
segs.e: Fear regarding livelihood, disrepute, feeling insecure in an assembly, death, and bad rebirth.

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Then that noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ ājīvikabhayassa bhāyāmi.
segs.e: ‘I have no fear regarding livelihood.

segs.p: Kissāhaṁ ājīvikabhayassa bhāyissāmi?
segs.e: Why would I be afraid of that?

segs.p: Atthi me cattāri balāni—
segs.e: I have these four powers:

segs.p: paññābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, anavajjabalaṁ, saṅgāhabalaṁ.
segs.e: the powers of wisdom, energy, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.

segs.p: Duppañño kho ājīvikabhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: A witless person might fear for their livelihood.

segs.p: Kusīto ājīvikabhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: A lazy person might fear for their livelihood.

segs.p: Sāvajjakāyakammantavacīkammantamanokammanto ājīvikabhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: Someone who does blameworthy things by way of body, speech, and mind might fear for their livelihood.

segs.p: Asaṅgāhako ājīvikabhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: Someone who does not include others might fear for their livelihood.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ asilokabhayassa bhāyāmi …pe…
segs.e: I have no fear of disrepute …

segs.p: nāhaṁ parisasārajjabhayassa bhāyāmi …pe…
segs.e: I have no fear about feeling insecure in an assembly …

segs.p: nāhaṁ maraṇabhayassa bhāyāmi …pe…
segs.e: I have no fear of death …

segs.p: nāhaṁ duggatibhayassa bhāyāmi.
segs.e: I have no fear of a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Kissāhaṁ duggatibhayassa bhāyissāmi?
segs.e: Why would I be afraid of that?

segs.p: Atthi me cattāri balāni—
segs.e: I have these four powers:

segs.p: paññābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, anavajjabalaṁ, saṅgāhabalaṁ.
segs.e: the powers of wisdom, energy, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.

segs.p: Duppañño kho duggatibhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: A witless person might be afraid of a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Kusīto duggatibhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: A lazy person might be afraid of a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Sāvajjakāyakammantavacīkammantamanokammanto duggatibhayassa bhāyeyya.
segs.e: Someone who does blameworthy things by way of body, speech, and mind might be afraid of a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Asaṅgāhako duggatibhayassa bhāyeyya’.
segs.e: Someone who does not include others might be afraid of a bad rebirth.’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi balehi samannāgato ariyasāvako imāni pañca bhayāni samatikkanto hotī”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four powers has got past these five fears.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Sevanāsutta
segs.e: Association

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi …pe… āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “Puggalopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: “Reverends, you should distinguish two two kinds of individual:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopi.
segs.e: those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.

segs.p: Cīvarampi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbaṁ—
segs.e: You should distinguish two kinds of robes:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampi.
segs.e: those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.

segs.p: Piṇḍapātopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: You should distinguish two kinds of almsfood:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopi.
segs.e: that which you should eat, and that which you shouldn’t eat.

segs.p: Senāsanampi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbaṁ—
segs.e: You should distinguish two kinds of lodging:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampi.
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.

segs.p: Gāmanigamopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: You should distinguish two kinds of village or town:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopi.
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.

segs.p: Janapadapadesopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: You should distinguish two kinds of country:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopi.
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.

segs.p: ‘Puggalopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two two kinds of individual:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā puggalaṁ:
segs.e: Well, should you know of an individual:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti;
segs.e: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.

segs.p: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca kasirena samudāgacchanti;
segs.e: And the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are hard to come by.

segs.p: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho na bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo rattibhāgaṁ vā divasabhāgaṁ vā saṅkhāpi anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṁ nānubandhitabbo.
segs.e: And the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is not being fully developed.’ In this case you should leave that individual at that very time of the day or night, without asking. You shouldn’t follow them.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā puggalaṁ:
segs.e: Whereas, should you know of an individual:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti;
segs.e: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.

segs.p: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca appakasirena samudāgacchanti;
segs.e: But the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are easy to come by.

segs.p: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho na bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo saṅkhāpi anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṁ nānubandhitabbo.
segs.e: However, the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is not being fully developed.’ In this case you should leave that individual after reflecting, without asking. You shouldn’t follow them.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā puggalaṁ:
segs.e: Well, should you know of an individual:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti;
segs.e: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.

segs.p: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca kasirena samudāgacchanti;
segs.e: And the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are hard to come by.

segs.p: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo saṅkhāpi anubandhitabbo na pakkamitabbaṁ.
segs.e: But the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is being fully developed.’ In this case you should follow that individual after appraisal. You shouldn’t leave them.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā puggalaṁ:
segs.e: Whereas, should you know of an individual:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti;
segs.e: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.

segs.p: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca appakasirena samudāgacchanti;
segs.e: And the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are easy to come by.

segs.p: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo yāvajīvaṁ anubandhitabbo na pakkamitabbaṁ api panujjamānena.
segs.e: And the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is being fully developed.’ In this case you should follow that individual. You shouldn’t leave them, even if they send you away.

segs.p: ‘Puggalopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of individual:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: ‘Cīvarampi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbaṁ—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of robes:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti,
segs.e: those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.’

segs.e: Well, should you know of a robe:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ kho me cīvaraṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṁ cīvaraṁ na sevitabbaṁ.
segs.e: ‘When I wear this robe, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.’ You should not wear that kind of robe.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā cīvaraṁ:
segs.e: Whereas, should you know of a robe:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ kho me cīvaraṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṁ cīvaraṁ sevitabbaṁ.
segs.e: ‘When I wear this robe, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should wear that kind of robe.

segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of robes:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti,
segs.e: those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: ‘Piṇḍapātopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of almsfood:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: that which you should eat, and that which you shouldn’t eat.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā piṇḍapātaṁ:
segs.e: Well, should you know of almsfood:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me piṇḍapātaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo piṇḍapāto na sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I eat this almsfood, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.’ You should not eat that kind of almsfood.

segs.e: Whereas, should you know of almsfood:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me piṇḍapātaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo piṇḍapāto sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I eat this almsfood, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should eat that kind of almsfood.

segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of almsfood:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: that which you should eat, and that which you shouldn’t eat.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: ‘Senāsanampi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbaṁ—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of lodging:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti,
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?

segs.e: Well, should you know of a lodging:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ kho me senāsanaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṁ senāsanaṁ na sevitabbaṁ.

segs.e: Whereas, should you know of a lodging:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ kho me senāsanaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṁ senāsanaṁ sevitabbaṁ.
segs.e: ‘When I frequent this lodging, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should frequent that kind of lodging.

segs.p: ‘Senāsanampi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbaṁ—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of lodging:

segs.p: sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti,
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.

segs.p: ‘Gāmanigamopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of village or town:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā gāmanigamaṁ:
segs.e: Well, should you know of a village or town:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me gāmanigamaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo gāmanigamo na sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I frequent this village or town, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.’ You should not frequent that kind of village or town.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā gāmanigamaṁ:
segs.e: Whereas, should you know of a village or town:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me gāmanigamaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo gāmanigamo sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I frequent this village or town, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should frequent that kind of village or town.

segs.p: ‘Gāmanigamopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of village or town:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.’

segs.p: ‘Janapadapadesopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of country:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,

segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā janapadapadesaṁ:
segs.e: Well, should you know of a country:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me janapadapadesaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo janapadapadeso na sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I frequent this country, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.’ You should not frequent that kind of country.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ jaññā janapadapadesaṁ:
segs.e: Whereas, should you know of a country:

segs.p: ‘imaṁ kho me janapadapadesaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo janapadapadeso sevitabbo.
segs.e: ‘When I frequent this country, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should frequent that kind of country.

segs.p: ‘Janapadapadesopi, āvuso, duvidhena veditabbo—
segs.e: ‘You should distinguish two kinds of country:

segs.p: sevitabbopi asevitabbopī’ti,
segs.e: those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.7
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.7

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Sutavāsutta
segs.e: With Sutavā the Wanderer

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho sutavā paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Sutavā went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho sutavā paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Ekamidāhaṁ, bhante, samayaṁ bhagavā idheva rājagahe viharāmi giribbaje.
segs.e: “Sir, this one time the Buddha was staying right here in Rājagaha, the Mountainfold.

segs.p: Tatra me, bhante, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: There I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘yo so, sutavā, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so pañca ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṁ—
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in five respects.

segs.p: abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṁ kāme paribhuñjituṁ seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto’ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a lay person.’

segs.p: Kacci metaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sussutaṁ suggahitaṁ sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritan”ti?
segs.e: I trust I properly heard, learned, applied the mind, and remembered that from the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Taggha te etaṁ, sutavā, sussutaṁ suggahitaṁ sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ.
segs.e: “Indeed, Sutavā, you properly heard, learned, applied the mind, and remembered that.

segs.p: Pubbe cāhaṁ, sutavā, etarahi ca evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: In the past, as today, I say this:

segs.p: ‘yo so bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so nava ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṁ—
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in nine respects.

segs.p: abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṁ kāme paribhuñjituṁ seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu chandāgatiṁ gantuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu dosāgatiṁ gantuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu mohāgatiṁ gantuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu bhayāgatiṁ gantuṁ’.
segs.e: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a lay person. And they can’t make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, or cowardice.’

segs.p: Pubbe cāhaṁ, sutavā, etarahi ca evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: In the past, as today, I say this:

segs.p: ‘yo so bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so imāni nava ṭhānāni ajjhācaritun’”ti.
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in these nine respects.’”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.8
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.8

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Sajjhasutta
segs.e: With the Wanderer Sajjha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho sajjho paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Sajjha went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho sajjho paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:
