segs.e: “Sir, this one time the Buddha was staying right here in Rājagaha, the Mountainfold.

segs.p: Tatra me, bhante, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: There I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘yo so, sajjha, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so pañca ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṁ—
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in five respects.

segs.p: abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṁ kāme paribhuñjituṁ seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto’ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a lay person.’

segs.p: Kacci metaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sussutaṁ suggahitaṁ sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritan”ti?
segs.e: I trust I properly heard, learned, applied the mind, and remembered that from the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Taggha te etaṁ, sajjha, sussutaṁ suggahitaṁ sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ.
segs.e: “Indeed, Sajjha, you properly heard, learned, applied the mind, and remembered that.

segs.p: Pubbe cāhaṁ, sajjha, etarahi ca evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: In the past, as today, I say this:

segs.p: ‘yo so bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so nava ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṁ—
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in nine respects.

segs.p: abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ …pe… abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṁ kāme paribhuñjituṁ seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu buddhaṁ paccakkhātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu dhammaṁ paccakkhātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu saṅghaṁ paccakkhātuṁ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sikkhaṁ paccakkhātuṁ’.
segs.e: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a lay person. And they can’t abandon the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, or the training.’

segs.p: Pubbe cāhaṁ, sajjha, etarahi ca evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: In the past, as today, I say this:

segs.p: ‘yo so bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, abhabbo so imāni nava ṭhānāni ajjhācaritun’”ti.
segs.e: ‘A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in these nine respects.’”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.9
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.9

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Puggalasutta
segs.e: Individuals

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these nine individuals are found in the world.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Arahā, arahattāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, puthujjano—
segs.e: The perfected one and the one practicing for perfection. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. And the ordinary person.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, nava puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine individuals found in the world.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.10
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.10

segs.p: 1. Sambodhivagga
segs.e: 1. Awakening

segs.p: Āhuneyyasutta
segs.e: Worthy of Offerings Dedicated to the Gods

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these nine individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Arahā, arahattāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, gotrabhū—
segs.e: The perfected one and the one practicing for perfection. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. And a lamb of the flock.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, nava puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Sambodhivaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Sambodhi nissayo ceva,
Meghiya nandakaṁ balaṁ;
Sevanā sutavā sajjho,
Puggalo āhuneyyena cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.11
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.11

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Sīhanādasutta
segs.e: Sāriputta’s Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “vuttho me, bhante, sāvatthiyaṁ vassāvāso.
segs.e: “Sir, I have completed the rainy season residence at Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Icchāmahaṁ, bhante, janapadacārikaṁ pakkamitun”ti.
segs.e: I wish to leave to wander the countryside.”

segs.p: “Yassadāni tvaṁ, sāriputta, kālaṁ maññasī”ti.
segs.e: “Please, Sāriputta, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Sāriputta rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu acirapakkante āyasmante sāriputte bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then, not long after Sāriputta had left, a certain monk said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “āyasmā maṁ, bhante, sāriputto āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkanto”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta attacked me and left without saying sorry.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena sāriputtaṁ āmantehi:
segs.e: “Please, monk, in my name tell Sāriputta that

segs.p: ‘satthā taṁ, āvuso sāriputta, āmantetī’”ti.
segs.e: the Teacher summons him.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to Sāriputta and said to him,

segs.p: “satthā taṁ, āvuso sāriputta, āmantetī”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, the Teacher summons you.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto tassa bhikkhuno paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Sāriputta replied.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca ānando avāpuraṇaṁ ādāya vihāre āhiṇḍanti:
segs.e: Now at that time the venerables Mahāmoggallāna and Ānanda, taking a latchkey, went from dwelling to dwelling, saying:

segs.p: “abhikkamathāyasmanto, abhikkamathāyasmanto.
segs.e: “Come forth, venerables! Come forth, venerables!

segs.p: Idānāyasmā sāriputto bhagavato sammukhā sīhanādaṁ nadissatī”ti.
segs.e: Now Venerable Sāriputta will roar his lion’s roar in the presence of the Buddha!”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “idha te, sāriputta, aññataro sabrahmacārī khīyanadhammaṁ āpanno:
segs.e: “Sāriputta, one of your spiritual companions has made this complaint:

segs.p: ‘āyasmā maṁ, bhante, sāriputto āsajja appaṭinissajjacārikaṁ pakkanto’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Venerable Sāriputta attacked me and left without saying sorry.’”

segs.p: “Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: “Sir, someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, pathaviyaṁ sucimpi nikkhipanti asucimpi nikkhipanti gūthagatampi nikkhipanti muttagatampi nikkhipanti kheḷagatampi nikkhipanti pubbagatampi nikkhipanti lohitagatampi nikkhipanti, na ca tena pathavī aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā;
segs.e: Suppose they were to toss both clean and unclean things on the earth, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The earth isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, pathavīsamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like the earth, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, āpasmiṁ sucimpi dhovanti asucimpi dhovanti gūthagatampi … muttagatampi … kheḷagatampi … pubbagatampi … lohitagatampi dhovanti, na ca tena āpo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā;
segs.e: Suppose they were to wash both clean and unclean things in water, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The water isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, āposamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like water, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, tejo sucimpi ḍahati asucimpi ḍahati gūthagatampi … muttagatampi … kheḷagatampi … pubbagatampi … lohitagatampi ḍahati, na ca tena tejo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā;
segs.e: Suppose a fire were to burn both clean and unclean things, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The fire isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, tejosamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like fire, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, vāyo sucimpi upavāyati asucimpi upavāyati gūthagatampi … muttagatampi … kheḷagatampi … pubbagatampi … lohitagatampi upavāyati, na ca tena vāyo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā;
segs.e: Suppose the wind was to blow on both clean and unclean things, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The wind isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, vāyosamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like the wind, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, rajoharaṇaṁ sucimpi puñchati asucimpi puñchati gūthagatampi … muttagatampi … kheḷagatampi … pubbagatampi … lohitagatampi puñchati, na ca tena rajoharaṇaṁ aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā;
segs.e: Suppose a rag was to wipe up both clean and unclean things, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The rag isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, rajoharaṇasamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like a rag, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, caṇḍālakumārako vā caṇḍālakumārikā vā kaḷopihattho nantakavāsī gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā pavisanto nīcacittaṁyeva upaṭṭhapetvā pavisati;
segs.e: Suppose a boy or girl of a corpse-worker tribe, holding a pot and clad in rags, were to enter a town or village. They’d enter with a humble mind.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, caṇḍālakumārakacaṇḍālakumārikāsamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like a boy or girl of a corpse-worker tribe, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, usabho chinnavisāṇo sūrato sudanto suvinīto rathiyāya rathiyaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ anvāhiṇḍanto na kiñci hiṁsati pādena vā visāṇena vā;
segs.e: Suppose there was a bull with his horns cut, gentle, well tamed and well trained. He’d wander from street to street and square to square without hurting anyone with his feet or horns.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, usabhachinnavisāṇasamena cetasā viharāmi vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: In the same way, I live with a heart like a bull with horns cut, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko sīsaṁnhāto ahikuṇapena vā kukkurakuṇapena vā manussakuṇapena vā kaṇṭhe āsattena aṭṭīyeyya harāyeyya jiguccheyya;
segs.e: Suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and had bathed their head. If the carcass of a snake or a dog or a human were hung around their neck, they’d be horrified, repelled, and disgusted.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, iminā pūtikāyena aṭṭīyāmi harāyāmi jigucchāmi.
segs.e: In the same way, I’m horrified, repelled, and disgusted by this rotting body.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyya.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, puriso medakathālikaṁ parihareyya chiddāvachiddaṁ uggharantaṁ paggharantaṁ;
segs.e: Suppose someone was to carry around a bowl of fat that was leaking and oozing from holes and cracks.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, imaṁ kāyaṁ pariharāmi chiddāvachiddaṁ uggharantaṁ paggharantaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, I carry around this body that’s leaking and oozing from holes and cracks.

segs.p: Yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṁ sabrahmacāriṁ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṁ pakkameyyā”ti.
segs.e: Someone who had not established mindfulness of the body might well attack one of their spiritual companions and leave without saying sorry.”

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then that monk rose from his seat, placed his robe over one shoulder, bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet, and said,

segs.p: “accayo maṁ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yo ahaṁ āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhiṁ.
segs.e: “I made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of me to speak ill of Venerable Sāriputta with an incorrect, hollow, false, untruthful claim.

segs.p: Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhatu āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please, sir, accept my mistake for what it is, so I will restrain myself in future.”

segs.p: “Taggha taṁ, bhikkhu, accayo accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yo tvaṁ sāriputtaṁ asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhi.
segs.e: “Indeed, monk, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to act in that way.

segs.p: Yato ca kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikarosi, taṁ te mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma.
segs.e: But since you have recognized your mistake for what it is, and have dealt with it properly, I accept it.

segs.p: Vuḍḍhihesā, bhikkhu, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikaroti āyatiṁ saṁvaraṁ āpajjatī”ti.
segs.e: For it is growth in the training of the Noble One to recognize a mistake for what it is, deal with it properly, and commit to restraint in the future.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta,

segs.p: “khama, sāriputta, imassa moghapurisassa, purā tassa tattheva sattadhā muddhā phalatī”ti.
segs.e: “Sāriputta, forgive that futile man before his head explodes into seven pieces right here.”

segs.p: “Khamāmahaṁ, bhante, tassa āyasmato sace maṁ so āyasmā evamāha:
segs.e: “I will pardon that venerable if he asks me:

segs.p: ‘khamatu ca me so āyasmā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘May the venerable please pardon me too.’”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.12
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.12

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Saupādisesasutta
segs.e: With Residue

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then it occurred to him,

segs.p: “atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya carituṁ,
segs.e: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī.

segs.p: yannūnāhaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then he went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together this discussion came up among them:

segs.p: “yo hi koci, āvuso, saupādiseso kālaṁ karoti, sabbo so aparimutto nirayā aparimutto tiracchānayoniyā aparimutto pettivisayā aparimutto apāyaduggativinipātā”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, no one who dies with residue is exempt from hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm. They’re not exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ bhāsitaṁ neva abhinandi nappaṭikkosi.
segs.e: Sāriputta neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions.

segs.p: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi:
segs.e: He rose from his seat, thinking,

segs.p: “bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājānissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi:
‘atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya carituṁ;
yannūnāhaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyan’ti.
Atha kho ahaṁ, bhante, yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodiṁ.
Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁ.
Tena kho pana samayena tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
‘yo hi koci, āvuso, saupādiseso kālaṁ karoti, sabbo so aparimutto nirayā aparimutto tiracchānayoniyā aparimutto pettivisayā aparimutto apāyaduggativinipātā’ti.
Atha kho ahaṁ, bhante, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ bhāsitaṁ neva abhinandiṁ nappaṭikkosiṁ.
Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁ:
‘bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājānissāmī’”ti.
“Ke ca, sāriputta, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bālā abyattā, ke ca saupādisesaṁ vā ‘saupādiseso’ti jānissanti, anupādisesaṁ vā ‘anupādiseso’ti jānissanti.
segs.e: “Sāriputta, these foolish, incompetent wanderers following other religions: who are they to know whether someone has residue or not?

segs.p: Navayime, sāriputta, puggalā saupādisesā kālaṁ kurumānā parimuttā nirayā parimuttā tiracchānayoniyā parimuttā pettivisayā parimuttā apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: There are these nine individuals who, dying with residue, are exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, ekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ paripūrakārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: There’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics and immersion, but has limited wisdom.

segs.p: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished between one life and the next.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, paṭhamo puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the first individual …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, idhekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ paripūrakārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics and immersion, but has limited wisdom.

segs.p: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished upon landing. This is the second individual …

segs.p: asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished without extra effort.
This is the third individual …

segs.p: sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished with extra effort.
This is the fourth individual …

segs.p: uddhaṁsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī.
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, pañcamo puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the fifth individual …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, idhekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ mattaso kārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics, but has limited immersion and wisdom.

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, they’re a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, chaṭṭho puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā …pe… parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the sixth individual …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, idhekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ mattaso kārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics, but has limited immersion and wisdom.

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā ekabījī hoti, ekaṁyeva mānusakaṁ bhavaṁ nibbattetvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters, they’re a one-seeder. They will be reborn just one time in a human existence, then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, sattamo puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā …pe… parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the seventh individual …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, idhekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ mattaso kārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics, but has limited immersion and wisdom.

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā kolaṅkolo hoti, dve vā tīṇi vā kulāni sandhāvitvā saṁsaritvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters, they go from family to family. They will transmigrate between two or three families and then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, aṭṭhamo puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā …pe… parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the eighth individual …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, idhekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ mattaso kārī, paññāya mattaso kārī.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s an individual who has fulfilled ethics, but has limited immersion and wisdom.

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sattakkhattuparamo hoti, sattakkhattuparamaṁ deve ca manusse ca sandhāvitvā saṁsaritvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters, they have at most seven rebirths. They will transmigrate at most seven times among gods and humans and then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, sāriputta, navamo puggalo saupādiseso kālaṁ kurumāno parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This is the ninth individual …

segs.p: Ke ca, sāriputta, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bālā abyattā, ke ca saupādisesaṁ vā ‘saupādiseso’ti jānissanti, anupādisesaṁ vā ‘anupādiseso’ti jānissanti.
segs.e: These foolish, incompetent wanderers following other religions: who are they to know whether someone has residue or not?

segs.p: Ime kho, sāriputta, nava puggalā saupādisesā kālaṁ kurumānā parimuttā nirayā parimuttā tiracchānayoniyā parimuttā pettivisayā parimuttā apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: These are the nine individuals who, dying with residue, are exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

segs.p: Na tāvāyaṁ, sāriputta, dhammapariyāyo paṭibhāsi bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ upāsakānaṁ upāsikānaṁ.
segs.e: Up until now, Sāriputta, I have not felt the need to give this exposition of the teaching to the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Māyimaṁ dhammapariyāyaṁ sutvā pamādaṁ āhariṁsūti.
segs.e: For I didn’t want those who heard it to introduce negligence.

segs.p: Api ca mayā, sāriputta, dhammapariyāyo pañhādhippāyena bhāsito”ti.
segs.e: However, I have spoken it in order to answer your question.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.13
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.13

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Koṭṭhikasutta
segs.e: With Koṭṭhita

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ samparāyavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced in this life be experienced by me in lives to come’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not, reverend.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ samparāyavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced in lives to come be experienced by me in this life’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ sukhavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ dukkhavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced as pleasant be experienced by me as painful’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panāvuso, sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ dukkhavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ sukhavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced as painful be experienced by me as pleasant’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ paripakkavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ aparipakkavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced when ripe be experienced by me when unripe’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ aparipakkavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ paripakkavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced when unripe be experienced by me when ripe’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ bahuvedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ appavedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced a lot be experienced by me a little’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ appavedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ bahuvedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced a little be experienced by me a lot’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ vedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ avedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds to be experienced by me be not experienced’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, ‘yaṁ kammaṁ avedanīyaṁ, taṁ me kammaṁ vedanīyaṁ hotū’ti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is the spiritual life led under the Buddha for this goal: ‘May deeds not to be experienced be experienced’?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “Certainly not.”

segs.p: “‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ samparāyavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, when you were asked whether the spiritual life was lived under the Buddha so that deeds to be experienced in this life are experienced in lives to come, you said, ‘Certainly not’.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ samparāyavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: When you were asked whether the spiritual life was lived under the Buddha so that deeds to be experienced in lives to come are experienced in this life …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ sukhavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ dukkhavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced as pleasant are experienced as painful …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ dukkhavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ sukhavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced as painful are experienced as pleasant …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ paripakkavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ aparipakkavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced when ripe are experienced when unripe …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ aparipakkavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ paripakkavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced when unripe are experienced when ripe …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ bahuvedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ appavedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced a lot are experienced a little …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ appavedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ bahuvedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced a little are experienced a lot …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ vedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ avedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: deeds to be experienced are not experienced …

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, yaṁ kammaṁ avedanīyaṁ taṁ me kammaṁ vedanīyaṁ hotūti, etassa atthāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: When you were asked whether the spiritual life was lived under the Buddha so that deeds not to be experienced are experienced, you said, ‘Certainly not.’

segs.p: Atha kimatthaṁ carahāvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti?
segs.e: Then what exactly is the goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Yaṁ khvassa, āvuso, aññātaṁ adiṭṭhaṁ appattaṁ asacchikataṁ anabhisametaṁ, tassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya abhisamayāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatīti.
segs.e: “Reverend, the spiritual life is lived under the Buddha to know, see, attain, realize, and comprehend that which is unknown, unseen, unattained, unrealized, and uncomprehended.”

segs.p: Kiṁ panassāvuso, aññātaṁ adiṭṭhaṁ appattaṁ asacchikataṁ anabhisametaṁ, yassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya abhisamayāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatīti?
segs.e: “But what is the unknown, unseen, unattained, unrealized, and uncomprehended?”

segs.p: ‘Idaṁ dukkhan’ti khvassa, āvuso, aññātaṁ adiṭṭhaṁ appattaṁ asacchikataṁ anabhisametaṁ.
segs.e: “‘This is suffering.’ …

segs.p: Tassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya abhisamayāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
‘Ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti khvassa, āvuso …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti khvassa, āvuso …pe…
segs.e: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ …

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti khvassa, āvuso, aññātaṁ adiṭṭhaṁ appattaṁ asacchikataṁ anabhisametaṁ.
segs.e: ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.’ …

segs.p: Tassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya abhisamayāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
Idaṁ khvassa, āvuso, aññātaṁ adiṭṭhaṁ appattaṁ asacchikataṁ anabhisametaṁ.
segs.e: This is the unknown, unseen, unattained, unrealized, and uncomprehended.

segs.p: Tassa ñāṇāya dassanāya pattiyā sacchikiriyāya abhisamayāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti.
segs.e: The spiritual life is lived under the Buddha to know, see, attain, realize, and comprehend this.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.14
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.14

segs.p: Samiddhisutta
segs.e: With Samiddhi

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ samiddhiṁ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Samiddhi went up to Venerable Sāriputta, bowed, and sat to one side. Venerable Sāriputta said to him:

segs.p: “Kimārammaṇā, samiddhi, purisassa saṅkappavitakkā uppajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “Samiddhi, based on what do thoughts arise in a person?”

segs.p: “Nāmarūpārammaṇā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Based on name and form, sir.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kva nānattaṁ gacchantī”ti?
segs.e: “Where do they become diversified?”

segs.p: “Dhātūsu, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “In the elements.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsamudayā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their origin?”

segs.p: “Phassasamudayā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Contact is their origin.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsamosaraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their meeting place?”

segs.p: “Vedanāsamosaraṇā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Feeling is their meeting place.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁpamukhā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their chief?”

segs.p: “Samādhippamukhā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Immersion is their chief.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁadhipateyyā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their ruler?”

segs.p: “Satādhipateyyā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Mindfulness is their ruler.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁuttarā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their overseer?”

segs.p: “Paññuttarā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Wisdom is their overseer.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsārā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their core?”

segs.p: “Vimuttisārā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Freedom is their core.”

segs.p: “Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁogadhā”ti?
segs.e: “What is their objective?”

segs.p: “Amatogadhā, bhante”ti.
segs.e: “Their objective is freedom from death.”

segs.p: “‘Kimārammaṇā, samiddhi, purisassa saṅkappavitakkā uppajjantī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘nāmarūpārammaṇā, bhante’ti vadesi.
segs.e: “Samiddhi, when you were asked what is the basis on which thoughts arise in a person, you answered ‘name and form’.

segs.p: ‘Te pana, samiddhi, kva nānattaṁ gacchantī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘dhātūsu, bhante’ti vadesi.
segs.e: When you were asked …

segs.p: ‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsamudayā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘phassasamudayā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsamosaraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘vedanāsamosaraṇā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁpamukhā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘samādhippamukhā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁadhipateyyā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘satādhipateyyā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁuttarā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘paññuttarā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁsārā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘vimuttisārā, bhante’ti vadesi.
‘Te pana, samiddhi, kiṁogadhā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘amatogadhā, bhante’ti vadesi.
segs.e: what is their objective, you answered ‘freedom from death’.

segs.p: Sādhu sādhu, samiddhi.
segs.e: Good, good, Samiddhi!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, samiddhi, puṭṭho puṭṭho vissajjesi, tena ca mā maññī”ti.
segs.e: It’s good that you answered each question. But don’t get conceited because of that.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.15
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.15

segs.p: Gaṇḍasutta
segs.e: The Simile of the Boil

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṇḍo anekavassagaṇiko.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose there was a boil that was many years old.

segs.p: Tassassu gaṇḍassa nava vaṇamukhāni nava abhedanamukhāni.
segs.e: And that boil had nine orifices that were continually open wounds.

segs.p: Tato yaṁ kiñci pagghareyya—
segs.e: Whatever oozed out of them

segs.p: asuciyeva pagghareyya, duggandhaṁyeva pagghareyya, jegucchiyaṁyeva pagghareyya;
segs.e: would be filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci pasaveyya—
segs.e: Whatever exuded from them

segs.p: asuciyeva pasaveyya, duggandhaṁyeva pasaveyya, jegucchiyaṁyeva pasaveyya.
segs.e: would be filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

segs.p: Gaṇḍoti kho, bhikkhave, imassetaṁ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṁ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammassa.
segs.e: ‘Boil’ is a term for this body made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

segs.p: Tassassu gaṇḍassa nava vaṇamukhāni nava abhedanamukhāni.
segs.e: And that boil has nine orifices that are continually open wounds.

segs.p: Tato yaṁ kiñci paggharati—
segs.e: Whatever oozes out of them

segs.p: asuciyeva paggharati, duggandhaṁyeva paggharati, jegucchiyaṁyeva paggharati;
segs.e: is filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci pasavati—
segs.e: Whatever exudes from them

segs.p: asuciyeva pasavati, duggandhaṁyeva pasavati, jegucchiyaṁyeva pasavati.
segs.e: is filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ kāye nibbindathā”ti.
segs.e: So, mendicants, have no illusion about this body.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.16
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.16

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Saññāsutta
segs.e: Perceptions

segs.p: “Navayimā, bhikkhave, saññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these nine perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. Their objective and culmination is freedom from death.

segs.p: Katamā nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of ugliness, death, repulsiveness of food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, impermanence, suffering in impermanence, not-self in suffering, giving up, and fading away.

segs.p: imā kho, bhikkhave, nava saññā, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: These nine perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. Their objective and culmination is freedom from death.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.17
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.17

segs.p: Kulasutta
segs.e: Families

segs.p: “Navahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā nālaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā nālaṁ nisīdituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, visiting a family with nine factors is not worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is not worthwhile.

segs.p: Katamehi navahi?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Na manāpena paccuṭṭhenti, na manāpena abhivādenti, na manāpena āsanaṁ denti, santamassa pariguhanti, bahukampi thokaṁ denti, paṇītampi lūkhaṁ denti, asakkaccaṁ denti no sakkaccaṁ, na upanisīdanti dhammassavanāya, bhāsitamassa na sussūsanti.
segs.e: They don’t politely rise, bow, or offer a seat. They hide what they have. Even when they have much they give little. Even when they have fine things they give coarse things. They give carelessly, not carefully. They don’t sit nearby to listen to the teachings. When you’re speaking, they don’t listen well.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, navahaṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā nālaṁ upagantuṁ upagantvā vā nālaṁ nisīdituṁ.
segs.e: Visiting a family with these nine factors is not worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is not worthwhile.

segs.p: Navahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā alaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā alaṁ nisīdituṁ.
segs.e: Visiting a family with nine factors is worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is worthwhile.

segs.p: Katamehi navahi?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Manāpena paccuṭṭhenti, manāpena abhivādenti, manāpena āsanaṁ denti, santamassa na pariguhanti, bahukampi bahukaṁ denti, paṇītampi paṇītaṁ denti, sakkaccaṁ denti no asakkaccaṁ, upanisīdanti dhammassavanāya, bhāsitamassa sussūsanti.
segs.e: They politely rise, bow, and offer a seat. They don’t hide what they have. When they have much they give much. When they have refined things they give refined things. They give carefully, not carelessly. They sit nearby to listen to the teachings. When you’re speaking, they listen well.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, navahaṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā alaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā alaṁ nisīditun”ti.
segs.e: Visiting a family with these nine factors is worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is worthwhile.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.18
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.18
