segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Navaṅguposathasutta
segs.e: The Sabbath with Nine Factors

segs.p: “Navahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato uposatho upavuttho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the observance of the sabbath with its nine factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

segs.p: Kathaṁ upavuttho ca, bhikkhave, navahaṅgehi samannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro?
segs.e: And how should it be observed?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yāvajīvaṁ arahanto pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā nihitadaṇḍā nihitasatthā lajjī dayāpannā sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampino viharanti;
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi; uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

segs.p: Iminā paṭhamena aṅgena samannāgato hoti …pe….
segs.e: This is its first factor. …

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭiviratā nīcaseyyaṁ kappenti—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā;
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato nīcaseyyaṁ kappemi—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi; uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

segs.p: Iminā aṭṭhamena aṅgena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: This is its eighth factor.

segs.p: Mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Iminā navamena aṅgena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: This is its ninth factor.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, bhikkhave, navahaṅgehi samannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro”ti.
segs.e: The observance of the sabbath with its nine factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.19
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.19

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Devatāsutta
segs.e: A Deity

segs.p: “Imañca, bhikkhave, rattiṁ sambahulā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, tā devatā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight, several glorious deities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:

segs.p: ‘upasaṅkamiṁsu no, bhante, pubbe manussabhūtānaṁ pabbajitā agārāni.
segs.e: ‘Sir, formerly when we were human beings, renunciates came to our homes.

segs.p: Te mayaṁ, bhante, paccuṭṭhimha, no ca kho abhivādimha.
segs.e: We politely rose for them, but we didn’t bow.

segs.p: Tā mayaṁ, bhante, aparipuṇṇakammantā vippaṭisāriniyo paccānutāpiniyo hīnaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā’ti.
segs.e: And so, having not fulfilled our duty, full of remorse and regret, we were reborn in a lesser realm.’

segs.p: Aparāpi maṁ, bhikkhave, sambahulā devatā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several other deities came to me and said:

segs.p: ‘upasaṅkamiṁsu no, bhante, pubbe manussabhūtānaṁ pabbajitā agārāni.
segs.e: ‘Sir, formerly when we were human beings, renunciates came to our homes.

segs.p: Te mayaṁ, bhante, paccuṭṭhimha abhivādimha, no ca tesaṁ āsanaṁ adamha.
segs.e: We politely rose for them and bowed, but we didn’t offer a seat.

segs.p: Tā mayaṁ, bhante, aparipuṇṇakammantā vippaṭisāriniyo paccānutāpiniyo hīnaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā’ti.
segs.e: And so, having not fulfilled our duty, full of remorse and regret, we were reborn in a lesser realm.’

segs.p: Aparāpi maṁ, bhikkhave, sambahulā devatā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several other deities came to me and said:

segs.p: ‘upasaṅkamiṁsu no, bhante, pubbe manussabhūtānaṁ pabbajitā agārāni.
segs.e: ‘Sir, formerly when we were human beings, renunciates came to our homes.

segs.p: Te mayaṁ, bhante, paccuṭṭhimha abhivādimha āsanaṁ adamha, no ca kho yathāsatti yathābalaṁ saṁvibhajimha …pe…
segs.e: We politely rose for them, bowed, and offered a seat, but we didn’t share as best we could. …’

segs.p: yathāsatti yathābalaṁ saṁvibhajimha, no ca kho upanisīdimha dhammassavanāya …pe…
segs.e: ‘… we didn’t sit nearby to listen to the teachings. …’

segs.p: upanisīdimha dhammassavanāya, no ca kho ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇimha …pe…
segs.e: ‘… we didn’t actively listen to the teachings. …’

segs.p: ohitasotā ca dhammaṁ suṇimha, no ca kho sutvā dhammaṁ dhārayimha …pe…
segs.e: ‘… we didn’t memorize the teachings. …’

segs.p: sutvā ca dhammaṁ dhārayimha, no ca kho dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhimha …pe…
segs.e: ‘… we didn’t examine the meaning of teachings we’d memorized. …’

segs.p: dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhimha, no ca kho atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammaṁ paṭipajjimha.
segs.e: ‘… not having understood the meaning and the teaching, we didn’t practice in line with the teaching.

segs.p: Tā mayaṁ, bhante, aparipuṇṇakammantā vippaṭisāriniyo paccānutāpiniyo hīnaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā’ti.
segs.e: And so, having not fulfilled our duty, full of remorse and regret, we were reborn in a lesser realm.’

segs.p: Aparāpi maṁ, bhikkhave, sambahulā devatā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several other deities came to me and said:

segs.p: ‘upasaṅkamiṁsu no, bhante, pubbe manussabhūtānaṁ pabbajitā agārāni.
segs.e: ‘Sir, formerly when we were human beings, renunciates came to our homes.

segs.p: Te mayaṁ, bhante, paccuṭṭhimha abhivādimha, āsanaṁ adamha, yathāsatti yathābalaṁ saṁvibhajimha, upanisīdimha dhammassavanāya, ohitasotā ca dhammaṁ suṇimha, sutvā ca dhammaṁ dhārayimha, dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhimha, atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammaṁ paṭipajjimha.
segs.e: We politely rose, bowed, and offered them a seat. We shared as best we could. We sat nearby to listen to the teachings, lent an ear, memorized them, and examined their meaning. Understanding the teaching and the meaning we practiced in line with the teaching.

segs.p: Tā mayaṁ, bhante, paripuṇṇakammantā avippaṭisāriniyo apaccānutāpiniyo paṇītaṁ kāyaṁ upapannā’ti.
segs.e: And so, having fulfilled our duty, free of remorse and regret, we were reborn in a superior realm.’

segs.p: Etāni, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlāni etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha seyyathāpi tā purimikā devatā”ti.
segs.e: Here, mendicants, are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicants! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later, like those former deities.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.20
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.20

segs.p: 2. Sīhanādavagga
segs.e: 2. The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: Velāmasutta
segs.e: About Velāma

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “Api nu te, gahapati, kule dānaṁ dīyatī”ti?
segs.e: “Householder, I wonder whether your family gives gifts?”

segs.p: “Dīyati me, bhante, kule dānaṁ;
segs.e: “It does, sir.

segs.p: tañca kho lūkhaṁ kaṇājakaṁ biḷaṅgadutiyan”ti.
segs.e: But only coarse sour gruel with false black pepper.”

segs.p: “Lūkhañcepi, gahapati, dānaṁ deti paṇītaṁ vā;
segs.e: “Householder, someone might give a gift that’s either coarse or fine.

segs.p: tañca asakkaccaṁ deti, acittīkatvā deti, asahatthā deti, apaviddhaṁ deti, anāgamanadiṭṭhiko deti.
segs.e: But they give it carelessly, thoughtlessly, not with their own hand. They give the dregs, and they give without consideration for consequences.

segs.p: Yattha yattha tassa tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, na uḷārāya bhattabhogāya cittaṁ namati, na uḷārāya vatthabhogāya cittaṁ namati, na uḷārāya yānabhogāya cittaṁ namati, na uḷāresu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu bhogāya cittaṁ namati.
segs.e: Then wherever the result of any such gift manifests, their mind doesn’t incline toward enjoyment of nice food, clothes, vehicles, or the five refined kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Yepissa te honti puttāti vā dārāti vā dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā, tepi na sussūsanti na sotaṁ odahanti na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti.
segs.e: And their children, wives, bondservants, servants, and workers don’t want to listen to them. They don’t actively listen or try to understand.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Evañhetaṁ, gahapati, hoti asakkaccaṁ katānaṁ kammānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: Because that is the result of deeds done carelessly.

segs.p: Lūkhañcepi, gahapati, dānaṁ deti paṇītaṁ vā;
segs.e: Someone might give a gift that’s either coarse or fine.

segs.p: tañca sakkaccaṁ deti, cittīkatvā deti, sahatthā deti, anapaviddhaṁ deti, āgamanadiṭṭhiko deti.
segs.e: And they give it carefully, thoughtfully, with their own hand. They don’t give the dregs, and they give with consideration for consequences.

segs.p: Yattha yattha tassa tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, uḷārāya bhattabhogāya cittaṁ namati, uḷārāya vatthabhogāya cittaṁ namati, uḷārāya yānabhogāya cittaṁ namati, uḷāresu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu bhogāya cittaṁ namati.
segs.e: Then wherever the result of any such gift manifests, their mind inclines toward enjoyment of nice food, clothes, vehicles, or the five refined kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Yepissa te honti puttāti vā dārāti vā dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā, tepi sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti.
segs.e: And their children, wives, bondservants, servants, and workers want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Evañhetaṁ, gahapati, hoti sakkaccaṁ katānaṁ kammānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: Because that is the result of deeds done carefully.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, gahapati, velāmo nāma brāhmaṇo ahosi.
segs.e: Once upon a time, householder, there was a brahmin named Velāma.

segs.p: So evarūpaṁ dānaṁ adāsi mahādānaṁ.
segs.e: He gave the following gift, a great offering.

segs.p: Caturāsīti suvaṇṇapātisahassāni adāsi rūpiyapūrāni, caturāsīti rūpiyapātisahassāni adāsi suvaṇṇapūrāni, caturāsīti kaṁsapātisahassāni adāsi hiraññapūrāni, caturāsīti hatthisahassāni adāsi sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālappaṭicchannāni, caturāsīti rathasahassāni adāsi sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālappaṭicchannāni, caturāsīti dhenusahassāni adāsi dukūlasandhanāni kaṁsūpadhāraṇāni, caturāsīti kaññāsahassāni adāsi āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalāyo, caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni adāsi gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni, caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni adāsi khomasukhumānaṁ koseyyasukhumānaṁ kambalasukhumānaṁ kappāsikasukhumānaṁ, ko pana vādo annassa pānassa khajjassa bhojjassa leyyassa peyyassa, najjo maññe vissandanti.
segs.e: 84,000 gold cups filled with silver. 84,000 silver cups filled with gold. 84,000 bronze cups filled with gold coins. 84,000 elephants with gold adornments and banners, covered with snow gold netting. 84,000 chariots upholstered with the hide of lions, tigers, and leopards, and cream rugs, with gold adornments and banners, covered with snow gold netting. 84,000 milk cows with muslin halter and bronze pails. 84,000 maidens bedecked with jeweled earrings. 84,000 couches spread with woolen covers—shag-piled, pure white, or embroidered with flowers—and spread with a fine deer hide, with canopies above and red pillows at both ends. 8,400,000,000 cloths of delicate linen, cotton, silk, and wool. And who can say how much food, drink, snacks, meals, refreshments, and beverages? It seemed like an overflowing river.

segs.p: Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘añño nūna tena samayena velāmo brāhmaṇo ahosi, so taṁ dānaṁ adāsi mahādānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Surely the brahmin Velāma must have been someone else at that time?’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Ahaṁ tena samayena velāmo brāhmaṇo ahosiṁ.
segs.e: I myself was the brahmin Velāma at that time.

segs.p: Ahaṁ taṁ dānaṁ adāsiṁ mahādānaṁ.
segs.e: I gave that gift, a great offering.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, gahapati, dāne na koci dakkhiṇeyyo ahosi, na taṁ koci dakkhiṇaṁ visodheti.
segs.e: But at that event there was no one worthy of a religious donation, and no one to purify the religious donation.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, velāmo brāhmaṇo dānaṁ adāsi mahādānaṁ, yo cekaṁ diṭṭhisampannaṁ bhojeyya, idaṁ tato mahapphalataraṁ.
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one individual accomplished in view than that great offering of Velāma.

segs.p: (…) Yo ca sataṁ diṭṭhisampannānaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ sakadāgāmiṁ bhojeyya, idaṁ tato mahapphalataraṁ.
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one once-returner than a hundred of those accomplished in view.

segs.p: (…) Yo ca sataṁ sakadāgāmīnaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ anāgāmiṁ bhojeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one non-returner than a hundred once-returners.

segs.p: yo ca sataṁ anāgāmīnaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ arahantaṁ bhojeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one perfected one than a hundred non-returners.

segs.p: yo ca sataṁ arahantānaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ paccekabuddhaṁ bhojeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one independent Buddha than a hundred perfected ones.

segs.p: yo ca sataṁ paccekabuddhānaṁ bhojeyya, yo ca tathāgataṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ bhojeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed one Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha than a hundred independent Buddhas.

segs.p: yo ca buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhojeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to feed the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha than to feed one Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: yo ca cātuddisaṁ saṅghaṁ uddissa vihāraṁ kārāpeyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to build a dwelling especially for the Saṅgha of the four quarters than to feed the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha.

segs.p: yo ca pasannacitto buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gaccheyya …pe…
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to go for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha with a confident heart than to build a dwelling for the Saṅgha of the four quarters.

segs.p: yo ca pasannacitto sikkhāpadāni samādiyeyya—
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to undertake the training rules—not to kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor—than to go for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha with a confident heart.

segs.p: pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṁ, adinnādānā veramaṇiṁ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiṁ, musāvādā veramaṇiṁ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiṁ, yo ca antamaso gandhohanamattampi mettacittaṁ bhāveyya, (…) idaṁ tato mahapphalataraṁ.
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to develop a heart of love—even just as long as it takes to pull a cow’s udder—than to undertake the training rules.

segs.p: Yañca, gahapati, velāmo brāhmaṇo dānaṁ adāsi mahādānaṁ, yo cekaṁ diṭṭhisampannaṁ bhojeyya …
segs.e: It would be more fruitful to develop the perception of impermanence—even as long as a finger-snap—than to do all of these things, including developing a heart of love for as long as it takes to pull a cow’s udder.”

segs.p: yo ca sataṁ diṭṭhisampannānaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ sakadāgāmiṁ bhojeyya …
yo ca sataṁ sakadāgāmīnaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ anāgāmiṁ bhojeyya …
yo ca sataṁ anāgāmīnaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ arahantaṁ bhojeyya …
yo ca sataṁ arahantānaṁ bhojeyya, yo cekaṁ paccekabuddhaṁ bhojeyya …
yo ca sataṁ paccekabuddhānaṁ bhojeyya, yo ca tathāgataṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ bhojeyya …
yo ca buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhojeyya, yo ca cātuddisaṁ saṅghaṁ uddissa vihāraṁ kārāpeyya …
yo ca pasannacitto buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gaccheyya, yo ca pasannacitto sikkhāpadāni samādiyeyya—

pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṁ …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiṁ, yo ca antamaso gandhohanamattampi mettacittaṁ bhāveyya, yo ca accharāsaṅghātamattampi aniccasaññaṁ bhāveyya, idaṁ tato mahapphalataran”ti.
Dasamaṁ.
Sīhanādavaggo dutiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Nādo saupādiseso ca,
koṭṭhikena samiddhinā;
Gaṇḍasaññā kulaṁ mettā,
devatā velāmena cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.21
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.21

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Tiṭhānasutta
segs.e: In Three Particulars

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, ṭhānehi uttarakurukā manussā deve ca tāvatiṁse adhiggaṇhanti jambudīpake ca manusse.
segs.e: “The humans of the land north of Kuru surpass the gods of the thirty-three and the humans of the Black Plum Tree Land in three particulars.

segs.p: Katamehi tīhi?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Amamā, apariggahā, niyatāyukā, visesaguṇā—
segs.e: They’re selfless and not possessive. They have a fixed lifespan. They have a distinctive nature.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi ṭhānehi uttarakurukā manussā deve ca tāvatiṁse adhiggaṇhanti jambudīpake ca manusse.
segs.e: The humans of the land north of Kuru surpass the gods of the thirty-three and the humans of the Black Plum Tree Land in these three particulars.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, ṭhānehi devā tāvatiṁsā uttarakuruke ca manusse adhiggaṇhanti jambudīpake ca manusse.
segs.e: The gods of the thirty-three surpass the humans of the land north of Kuru and the Black Plum Tree Land in three particulars.

segs.p: Katamehi tīhi?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena—
segs.e: Heavenly lifespan, beauty, and happiness.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi ṭhānehi devā tāvatiṁsā uttarakuruke ca manusse adhiggaṇhanti jambudīpake ca manusse.
segs.e: The gods of the thirty-three surpass the humans of the land north of Kuru and the Black Plum Tree Land in these three particulars.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, ṭhānehi jambudīpakā manussā uttarakuruke ca manusse adhiggaṇhanti deve ca tāvatiṁse.
segs.e: The humans of the Black Plum Tree Land surpass the humans of the land north of Kuru and the gods of the thirty-three in three particulars.

segs.p: Katamehi tīhi?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Sūrā, satimanto, idha brahmacariyavāso—
segs.e: Bravery, mindfulness, and the spiritual life is lived here.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi ṭhānehi jambudīpakā manussā uttarakuruke ca manusse adhiggaṇhanti deve ca tāvatiṁse”ti.
segs.e: The humans of the Black Plum Tree Land surpass the humans of the land north of Kuru and the gods of the thirty-three in these three particulars.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.22
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.22

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Assakhaḷuṅkasutta
segs.e: A Wild Colt

segs.p: “Tayo ca, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅke desessāmi tayo ca purisakhaḷuṅke tayo ca assaparasse tayo ca purisaparasse tayo ca bhadde assājānīye tayo ca bhadde purisājānīye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you about three wild colts and three wild people; three excellent horses and three excellent people; and three fine thoroughbred horses and three fine thoroughbred people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha. (…)
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo assakhaḷuṅkā?
segs.e: And what are the three wild colts?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti, na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One wild colt is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another wild colt is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another wild colt is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo assakhaḷuṅkā.
segs.e: These are the three wild colts.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo purisakhaḷuṅkā?
segs.e: And what are the three wild people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti, na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One wild person is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another wild person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another wild person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti, na vaṇṇasampanno na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Idamassa javasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho saṁsādeti, no vissajjeti.
segs.e: But when asked a question about the teaching or training, they falter without answering.

segs.p: Idamassa na vaṇṇasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re not beautiful, I say.

segs.p: Na kho pana lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: And they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa na ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti, na vaṇṇasampanno na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Idamassa javasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.

segs.p: Idamassa vaṇṇasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re beautiful, I say.

segs.p: Na kho pana lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: But they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa na ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Idamassa javasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.

segs.p: Idamassa vaṇṇasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re beautiful, I say.

segs.p: Lābhī kho pana hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo purisakhaḷuṅkā.
segs.e: These are the three wild people.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo assaparassā?
segs.e: And what are the three excellent horses?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assaparasso …pe…
segs.e: One excellent horse …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo assaparassā.
segs.e: These are the three excellent horses.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo purisaparassā?
segs.e: What are the three excellent people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco purisaparasso …pe…
segs.e: One excellent person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisaparasso …pe…
segs.e: And how is an excellent person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti, tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, with the ending of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

segs.p: Idamassa javasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.

segs.p: Idamassa vaṇṇasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re beautiful, I say.

segs.p: Lābhī kho pana hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how an excellent person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo purisaparassā.
segs.e: These are the three excellent people.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo bhaddā assājānīyā?
segs.e: And what are the three fine thoroughbred horses?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco bhaddo assājānīyo …pe…
segs.e: One fine thoroughbred horse …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo bhaddā assājānīyā.
segs.e: These are the three fine thoroughbred horses.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo bhaddā purisājānīyā?
segs.e: And what are the three fine thoroughbred people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco bhaddo purisājānīyo …pe…
segs.e: One fine thoroughbred person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhaddo purisājānīyo …pe…
segs.e: And how is a fine thoroughbred person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Idamassa javasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.

segs.p: Idamassa vaṇṇasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re beautiful, I say.

segs.p: Lābhī kho pana hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhaddo purisājānīyo javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how a fine thoroughbred person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo bhaddā purisājānīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three fine thoroughbred people.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.23
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.23

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Taṇhāmūlakasutta
segs.e: Rooted in Craving

segs.p: “Nava, bhikkhave, taṇhāmūlake dhamme desessāmi, taṁ suṇātha.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you about nine things rooted in craving.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā?
segs.e: And what are the nine things rooted in craving?

segs.p: Taṇhaṁ paṭicca pariyesanā, pariyesanaṁ paṭicca lābho, lābhaṁ paṭicca vinicchayo, vinicchayaṁ paṭicca chandarāgo, chandarāgaṁ paṭicca ajjhosānaṁ, ajjhosānaṁ paṭicca pariggaho, pariggahaṁ paṭicca macchariyaṁ, macchariyaṁ paṭicca ārakkho, ārakkhādhikaraṇaṁ daṇḍādānaṁ satthādānaṁ kalahaviggahavivādatuvaṁtuvaṁpesuññamusāvādā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: Craving gives rise to searching. Searching gives rise to gaining material things. Gaining material things gives rise to evaluation. Evaluation gives rise to desire and lust. Desire and lust gives rise to attachment. Attachment gives rise to ownership. Ownership gives rise to stinginess. Stinginess gives rise to safeguarding. Owing to safeguarding, many bad, unskillful things come to be: taking up the rod and the sword, quarrels, arguments, and disputes, accusations, backbiting, and lies.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine things rooted in craving.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.24
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.24

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Sattāvāsasutta
segs.e: Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, sattāvāsā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are nine abodes of sentient beings.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā, ekacce ca devā, ekacce ca vinipātikā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

segs.p: Ayaṁ paṭhamo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the first abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

segs.p: Ayaṁ dutiyo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the second abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of sublime luminosity.

segs.p: Ayaṁ tatiyo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the third abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

segs.p: Ayaṁ catuttho sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the fourth abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā asaññino appaṭisaṁvedino, seyyathāpi devā asaññasattā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that are non-percipient and do not experience anything, such as the gods who are non-percipient beings.

segs.p: Ayaṁ pañcamo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the fifth abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Ayaṁ chaṭṭho sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the sixth abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ sattamo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the seventh abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ aṭṭhamo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the eighth abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, sattā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā.
segs.e: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of nothingness. They have been reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ayaṁ navamo sattāvāso.
segs.e: This is the ninth abode of sentient beings.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, nava sattāvāsā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine abodes of sentient beings.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.25
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.25

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Paññāsutta
segs.e: Consolidated by Wisdom

segs.p: “Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kallaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant’s mind has been well consolidated with wisdom it’s appropriate for them to say:

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is a mendicant’s mind well consolidated with wisdom?

segs.p: ‘Vītarāgaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: The mind is well consolidated with wisdom when they know: ‘My mind is without greed.’

segs.p: ‘vītadosaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is without hate.’

segs.p: ‘vītamohaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is without delusion.’

segs.p: ‘asarāgadhammaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become greedy.’

segs.p: ‘asadosadhammaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become hateful.’

segs.p: ‘asamohadhammaṁ me cittan’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become deluded.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ kāmabhavāyā’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the sensual realm.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ rūpabhavāyā’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the realm of luminous form.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ arūpabhavāyā’ti paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti.
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the formless realm.’

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paññāya cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kallaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: When a mendicant’s mind has been well consolidated with wisdom it’s appropriate for them to say:

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Silāyūpasutta
segs.e: The Simile of the Stone Post
So I have heard.

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca candikāputto rājagahe viharanti veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi (…):
segs.e: There Venerable Candikāputta addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: “Reverends, Devadatta teaches the mendicants like this:

segs.p: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
segs.e: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is solidified by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to him,

segs.p: “na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: “Reverend Candikāputta, Devadatta does not teach the mendicants like that.

segs.p: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso, candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: He teaches like this:

segs.p: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
segs.e: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is well consolidated by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: For a second time …

segs.p: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Dutiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
“na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: And for a third time Venerable Candikāputta addressed the mendicants …

segs.p: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time, Sāriputta said to him,

segs.p: “na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: “Reverend Candikāputta, Devadatta does not teach the mendicants like that.

segs.p: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: He teaches like this:

segs.p: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
segs.e: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is well consolidated by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’

segs.p: Kathañca, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is a mendicant’s mind well consolidated by heart?

segs.p: ‘Vītarāgaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: The mind is well consolidated by heart when they know: ‘My mind is without greed.’

segs.p: ‘vītadosaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is without hate.’

segs.p: ‘vītamohaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is without delusion.’

segs.p: ‘asarāgadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become greedy.’

segs.p: ‘asadosadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become hateful.’

segs.p: ‘asamohadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to become deluded.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ kāmabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the sensual realm.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ rūpabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the realm of luminous form.’

segs.p: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ arūpabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti.
segs.e: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the formless realm.’

segs.p: Evaṁ sammā vimuttacittassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
segs.e: When a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t occupy their mind.

segs.p: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassati.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, silāyūpo soḷasakukkuko.
segs.e: Suppose there was a stone post, sixteen feet long.

segs.p: Tassassu aṭṭha kukkū heṭṭhā nemaṅgamā, aṭṭha kukkū upari nemassa.
segs.e: Eight feet were buried underground, and eight above ground.

segs.p: Atha puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampavedheyya;
segs.e: And violent storms were to blow up out of the east, the west, the north, and the south.

segs.p: atha pacchimāya …
atha uttarāya …
atha dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampavedheyya.
segs.e: They couldn’t make it tremor and tremble and quake.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Gambhīrattā, āvuso, nemassa, sunikhātattā silāyūpassa.
segs.e: It’s because that stone post is firmly embedded, with deep foundations.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, sammā vimuttacittassa bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t occupy their mind.

segs.p: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassati.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

segs.p: Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā …
segs.e: If even compelling sounds …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: smells …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: tastes …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā …
segs.e: touches …

segs.p: manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
segs.e: and ideas come into the range of the mind they don’t occupy the mind.

segs.p: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassatī”ti.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.

segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.27

segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Paṭhamaverasutta
segs.e: Fears and Enmities (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, and possesses the four factors of stream-entry, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

segs.p: Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti?
segs.e: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, pāṇātipātā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from killing living creatures does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, adinnādāyī …pe…
segs.e: Anyone who steals …

segs.p: kāmesumicchācārī …
segs.e: Anyone who commits sexual misconduct …

segs.p: musāvādī …
segs.e: Anyone who lies …

segs.p: surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

segs.p: Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.
segs.e: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.

segs.p: “Katamehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti?
segs.e: What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho; yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi ca catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled these five fears and enmities, and possesses these four factors of stream-entry, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.

segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.28

Dhamme …pe…
segs.e: the teaching …

segs.p: saṅghe …
segs.e: the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi ca catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled these five fears and enmities, and possesses these four factors of stream-entry, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.29
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.29

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Āghātavatthusutta
segs.e: Grounds for Resentment

segs.p: “Navayimāni, bhikkhave, āghātavatthūni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are nine grounds for resentment.

segs.p: Katamāni nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: ‘Anatthaṁ me acarī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati;
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me,’ you harbor resentment.

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me caratī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati;
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me carissatī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati;
segs.e: ‘They will do wrong to me’ …

segs.p: ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṁ acarī’ti …pe…
segs.e: ‘They did wrong to someone I love’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ caratī’ti …pe…
segs.e: ‘They are doing wrong to someone I love’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ carissatī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati;
segs.e: ‘They will do wrong to someone I love’ …

segs.p: ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṁ acarī’ti …pe…
segs.e: ‘They helped someone I dislike’ …

segs.p: ‘atthaṁ caratī’ti …pe…
segs.e: ‘They are helping someone I dislike’ …

segs.p: ‘atthaṁ carissatī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike,’ you harbor resentment.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, nava āghātavatthūnī”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine grounds for resentment.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.30
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.30

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Āghātapaṭivinayasutta
segs.e: Getting Rid of Resentment

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, āghātapaṭivinayā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these nine ways to get rid of resentment.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: ‘Anatthaṁ me acari, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They harmed me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me carati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They are harming me …’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;
segs.e: ‘They will harm me …’ …

segs.p: piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṁ acari …pe…
segs.e: ‘They harmed someone I love …’ …

segs.p: anatthaṁ carati …pe…
segs.e: ‘They are harming someone I love …’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;
segs.e: ‘They will harm someone I love …’ …

segs.p: appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṁ acari …pe…
segs.e: ‘They helped someone I dislike …’ …

segs.p: atthaṁ carati …pe…
segs.e: ‘They are helping someone I dislike …’ …

segs.p: ‘atthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, nava āghātapaṭivinayā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine ways to get rid of resentment.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.31
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.31

segs.p: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
segs.e: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

segs.p: Anupubbanirodhasutta
segs.e: Progressive Cessations

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, anupubbanirodhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these nine progressive cessations.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa kāmasaññā niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the first absorption, sensual perceptions have ceased.

segs.p: dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā honti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the second absorption, the placing of the mind and keeping it connected have ceased.

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa pīti niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the third absorption, rapture has ceased.

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa assāsapassāsā niruddhā honti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the fourth absorption, breathing has ceased.

segs.p: ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samāpannassa rūpasaññā niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite space, the perception of form has ceased.

segs.p: viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite consciousness, the perception of the dimension of infinite space has ceased.

segs.p: ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the dimension of nothingness, the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness has ceased.

segs.p: nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti;
segs.e: For someone who has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.

segs.p: saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā honti.
segs.e: For someone who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, nava anupubbanirodhā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine progressive cessations.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Sattāvāsavaggo tatiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Tiṭhānaṁ khaḷuṅko taṇhā,
Sattapaññā silāyupo;
Dve verā dve āghātāni,
Anupubbanirodhena cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.32
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.32

segs.p: 4. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 4. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Anupubbavihārasutta
segs.e: Progressive Meditations

segs.p: “Navayime, bhikkhave, anupubbavihārā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these nine progressive meditations.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ, dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ, tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ, catutthaṁ jhānaṁ, ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ, viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ, ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ, saññāvedayitanirodho—
segs.e: The first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption, the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness, the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and the cessation of perception and feeling.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, nava anupubbavihārā”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine progressive meditations.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.33
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.33

segs.p: 4. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 4. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Anupubbavihārasamāpattisutta
segs.e: The Nine Progressive Meditative Attainments

segs.p: “Navayimā, bhikkhave, anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo desessāmi, taṁ suṇātha …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the nine progressive meditative attainments …

segs.p: katamā ca, bhikkhave, nava anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo?
segs.e: And what are the nine progressive meditative attainments?

segs.p: Yattha kāmā nirujjhanti, ye ca kāme nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where sensual pleasures cease, and those who have thoroughly ended sensual pleasures meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha kāmā nirujjhanti, ke ca kāme nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where sensual pleasures cease’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, it’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Ettha kāmā nirujjhanti, te ca kāme nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where sensual pleasures cease.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha vitakkavicārā nirujjhanti, ye ca vitakkavicāre nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where the placing of the mind and keeping it connected cease, and those who have thoroughly ended the placing of the mind and keeping it connected meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha vitakkavicārā nirujjhanti, ke ca vitakkavicāre nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where the placing of the mind and keeping it connected cease’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: ettha vitakkavicārā nirujjhanti, te ca vitakkavicāre nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where the placing of the mind and keeping it connected cease.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha pīti nirujjhati, ye ca pītiṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where rapture ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended rapture meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha pīti nirujjhati, ke ca pītiṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where rapture ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, with the fading away of rapture, enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, “Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss”.

segs.p: ettha pīti nirujjhati, te ca pītiṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where rapture ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha upekkhāsukhaṁ nirujjhati, ye ca upekkhāsukhaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where bliss with equanimity ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended bliss with equanimity meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha upekkhāsukhaṁ nirujjhati, ke ca upekkhāsukhaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where bliss with equanimity ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: ettha upekkhāsukhaṁ nirujjhati, te ca upekkhāsukhaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where bliss with equanimity ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha rūpasaññā nirujjhati, ye ca rūpasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where perceptions of form ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended perceptions of form meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha rūpasaññā nirujjhati, ke ca rūpasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where perceptions of form ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that “space is infinite”, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Ettha rūpasaññā nirujjhati, te ca rūpasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where perceptions of form cease.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ye ca ākāsānañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where the perception of the dimension of infinite space ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended the perception of the dimension of infinite space meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ke ca ākāsānañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where the perception of the dimension of infinite space ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma anantaṁ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that “consciousness is infinite”, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segs.p: Ettha ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, te ca ākāsānañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where the perception of the dimension of infinite space ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ye ca viññāṇañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ke ca viññāṇañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that “there is nothing at all”, enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ettha viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, te ca viññāṇañcāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ye ca ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where the perception of the dimension of nothingness ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended the perception of the dimension of nothingness meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ke ca ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where the perception of the dimension of nothingness ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ettha ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, te ca ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where the perception of the dimension of nothingness ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Yattha nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ye ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti, ‘addhā te āyasmanto nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā pāraṅgatā tadaṅgenā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where the perception of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception ceases, and those who have thoroughly ended the perception of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception meditate, I say: ‘Clearly those venerables are desireless, quenched, crossed over, and gone beyond in that respect.’

segs.p: ‘Kattha nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, ke ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharanti—
segs.e: If someone should say, ‘I do not know or see where the perception of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception ceases’,

segs.p: ahametaṁ na jānāmi ahametaṁ na passāmī’ti, iti yo evaṁ vadeyya, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: they should be told:

segs.p: ‘idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling.

segs.p: Ettha nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā nirujjhati, te ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṁ nirodhetvā nirodhetvā viharantī’ti.
segs.e: That’s where the perception of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception ceases.’

segs.p: Addhā, bhikkhave, asaṭho amāyāvī ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinandeyya anumodeyya;
segs.e: Clearly someone who is not devious or deceitful would approve and agree with that statement.

segs.p: ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā namassamāno pañjaliko payirupāseyya.
segs.e: They’d say ‘Good!’ and bowing down, they’d pay homage with cupped palms.

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, nava anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo”ti.
segs.e: These are the nine progressive meditative attainments.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.34
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.34
