segs.p: Lokāyatikasutta
segs.e: Brahmin Cosmologists

segs.p: Atha kho dve lokāyatikā brāhmaṇā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then two brahmin cosmologists went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te brāhmaṇā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Pūraṇo, bho gotama, kassapo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, Pūraṇa Kassapa claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing, to know and see everything without exception, thus:

segs.p: ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṁ samitaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paccupaṭṭhitan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Knowledge and vision are constantly and continually present to me, while walking, standing, sleeping, and waking.’

segs.p: So evamāha:
segs.e: He says:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ anantena ñāṇena anantaṁ lokaṁ jānaṁ passaṁ viharāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘With infinite knowledge I know and see that the cosmos is infinite.’

segs.p: Ayampi, bho gotama, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: And the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan also claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing, to know and see everything without exception, thus:

segs.p: ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṁ samitaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paccupaṭṭhitan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Knowledge and vision are constantly and continually present to me, while walking, standing, sleeping, and waking.’

segs.p: So evamāha:
segs.e: He says:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ anantena ñāṇena anantaṁ lokaṁ jānaṁ passaṁ viharāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘With infinite knowledge I know and see that the cosmos is finite.’

segs.p: Imesaṁ, bho gotama, ubhinnaṁ ñāṇavādānaṁ ubhinnaṁ aññamaññaṁ vipaccanīkavādānaṁ ko saccaṁ āha ko musā”ti?
segs.e: These two claim to speak from knowledge, but they directly contradict each other. Which one of them speaks the truth, and which falsehood?”

segs.p: “Alaṁ, brāhmaṇā.
segs.e: “Enough, brahmins, let that be.

segs.p: Tiṭṭhatetaṁ:
‘imesaṁ ubhinnaṁ ñāṇavādānaṁ ubhinnaṁ aññamaññaṁ vipaccanīkavādānaṁ ko saccaṁ āha ko musā’ti.
Dhammaṁ vo, brāhmaṇā, desessāmi,
segs.e: I will teach you the Dhamma.

segs.p: taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho te brāhmaṇā bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” those brahmins replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇā, cattāro purisā catuddisā ṭhitā paramena javena ca samannāgatā paramena ca padavītihārena.
segs.e: “Suppose there were four men standing in the four quarters. Each of them was extremely fast, with an extremely mighty stride.

segs.p: Te evarūpena javena samannāgatā assu, seyyathāpi nāma daḷhadhammā dhanuggaho sikkhito katahattho katūpāsano lahukena asanena appakasirena tiriyaṁ tālacchāyaṁ atipāteyya;
segs.e: They’re as fast as a light arrow easily shot across the shadow of a palm tree by a well-trained expert archer with a strong bow.

segs.p: evarūpena ca padavītihārena, seyyathāpi nāma puratthimā samuddā pacchimo samuddo
segs.e: Their stride was such that it spanned from the eastern ocean to the western ocean.

segs.p: atha puratthimāya disāya ṭhito puriso evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Then the man standing in the east would say:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ pāpuṇissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’

segs.p: So aññatreva asitapītakhāyitasāyitā aññatra uccārapassāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṁ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṁ antarā kālaṁ kareyya.
segs.e: Though he’d travel for his whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—he’d die along the way, never reaching the end of the world.

segs.p: Atha pacchimāya disāya …pe…
segs.e: Then the man standing in the west …

segs.p: atha uttarāya disāya …
segs.e: Then the man standing in the north …

segs.p: atha dakkhiṇāya disāya ṭhito puriso evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Then the man standing in the south would say:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ pāpuṇissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’

segs.p: So aññatreva asitapītakhāyitasāyitā aññatra uccārapassāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṁ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṁ antarā kālaṁ kareyya.
segs.e: Though he’d travel for his whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—he’d die along the way, never reaching the end of the world.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, brāhmaṇā, evarūpāya sandhāvanikāya lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by running like this.

segs.p: Na cāhaṁ, brāhmaṇā, appatvāva lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.

segs.p: Pañcime, brāhmaṇā, kāmaguṇā ariyassa vinaye lokoti vuccati.
segs.e: These five kinds of sensual stimulation are called the world in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā;
segs.e: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: sotaviññeyyā saddā …pe…
segs.e: Sounds known by the ear …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: Smells known by the nose …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: Tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā;
segs.e: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: ime kho, brāhmaṇā, pañca kāmaguṇā ariyassa vinaye lokoti vuccati.
segs.e: These five kinds of sensual stimulation are called the world in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇā, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇā, ‘bhikkhu lokassa antamāgamma, lokassa ante viharati’.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world.

segs.p: Tamaññe evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: Others say of them:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Ahampi hi, brāhmaṇā, evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: And I also say this:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇā, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption …

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: third absorption …

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: fourth absorption.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇā, ‘bhikkhu lokassa antamāgamma lokassa ante viharati’.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world.

segs.p: Tamaññe evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: Others say of them:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Ahampi hi, brāhmaṇā, evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: And I also say this:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇā, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇā, ‘bhikkhu lokassa antamāgamma lokassa ante viharati’.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world.

segs.p: Tamaññe evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: Others say of them:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Ahampi hi, brāhmaṇā, evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: And I also say this:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇā, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …

segs.p: sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …pe…
segs.e: the dimension of nothingness …

segs.p: sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇā, ‘bhikkhu lokassa antamāgamma lokassa ante viharati’.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world.

segs.p: Tamaññe evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: Others say of them:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Ahampi hi, brāhmaṇā, evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: And I also say this:

segs.p: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇā, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, brāhmaṇā, ‘bhikkhu lokassa antamāgamma lokassa ante viharati tiṇṇo loke visattikan’”ti.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world. And they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.39
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.39

segs.p: 4. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 4. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Devāsurasaṅgāmasutta
segs.e: The War Between the Gods and the Titans

segs.p: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi.
segs.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme asurā jiniṁsu, devā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: In that battle the titans won and the gods lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, devā apayiṁsuyeva uttarenābhimukhā, abhiyiṁsu asurā.
segs.e: Defeated, the gods fled north with the titans in pursuit.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the gods thought,

segs.p: ‘abhiyanteva kho asurā.
segs.e: ‘The titans are still in pursuit.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ dutiyampi asurehi saṅgāmeyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we engage them in battle a second time?’

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, devā asurehi saṅgāmesuṁ.
segs.e: And so a second battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, asurāva jiniṁsu, devā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: And for a second time the titans won and the gods lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, devā apayiṁsuyeva uttarenābhimukhā, abhiyiṁsu asurā.
segs.e: Defeated, the gods fled north with the titans in pursuit.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the gods thought,

segs.p: ‘abhiyanteva kho asurā.
segs.e: ‘The titans are still in pursuit.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ tatiyampi asurehi saṅgāmeyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we engage them in battle a third time?’

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, devā asurehi saṅgāmesuṁ.
segs.e: And so a third battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, asurāva jiniṁsu, devā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: And for a third time the titans won and the gods lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, devā bhītā devapuraṁyeva pavisiṁsu.
segs.e: Defeated and terrified, the gods fled right into the castle of the gods.

segs.p: Devapuragatānañca pana, bhikkhave, devānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: When they had entered their castle, they thought,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni mayaṁ etarahi attanā viharāma akaraṇīyā asurehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now we’re in a secure location and the titans can’t do anything to us.’

segs.p: Asurānampi, bhikkhave, etadahosi:
segs.e: The titans also thought,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni devā etarahi attanā viharanti akaraṇīyā amhehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now the gods are in a secure location and we can’t do anything to them.’

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi.
segs.e: Once upon a time, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme devā jiniṁsu, asurā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: In that battle the gods won and the titans lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, asurā apayiṁsuyeva dakkhiṇenābhimukhā, abhiyiṁsu devā.
segs.e: Defeated, the titans fled south with the gods in pursuit.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, asurānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the titans thought,

segs.p: ‘abhiyanteva kho devā.
segs.e: ‘The gods are still in pursuit.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ dutiyampi devehi saṅgāmeyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we engage them in battle a second time?’

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, asurā devehi saṅgāmesuṁ.
segs.e: And so a second battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, devā jiniṁsu, asurā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: And for a second time the gods won and the titans lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, asurā apayiṁsuyeva dakkhiṇenābhimukhā, abhiyiṁsu devā.
segs.e: Defeated, the titans fled south with the gods in pursuit.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, asurānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the titans thought,

segs.p: ‘abhiyanteva kho devā.
segs.e: ‘The gods are still in pursuit.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ tatiyampi devehi saṅgāmeyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we engage them in battle a third time?’

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, asurā devehi saṅgāmesuṁ.
segs.e: And so a third battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, devā jiniṁsu, asurā parājayiṁsu.
segs.e: And for a third time the gods won and the titans lost.

segs.p: Parājitā ca, bhikkhave, asurā bhītā asurapuraṁyeva pavisiṁsu.
segs.e: Defeated and terrified, the titans fled right into the citadel of the titans.

segs.p: Asurapuragatānañca pana, bhikkhave, asurānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: When they had entered their citadel, they thought,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni mayaṁ etarahi attanā viharāma akaraṇīyā devehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now we’re in a secure location and the gods can’t do anything to us.’

segs.p: Devānampi, bhikkhave, etadahosi:
segs.e: And the gods also thought,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni asurā etarahi attanā viharanti akaraṇīyā amhehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now the titans are in a secure location and we can’t do anything to them.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati,
segs.e: In the same way, there’s a time when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhussa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: At that time the mendicant thinks,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dānāhaṁ etarahi attanā viharāmi akaraṇīyo mārassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now I’m in a secure location and Māra can’t do anything to me.’

segs.p: Mārassāpi, bhikkhave, pāpimato evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And Māra the Wicked also thinks,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni bhikkhu etarahi attanā viharati akaraṇīyo mayhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now the mendicant is in a secure location and we can’t do anything to them.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: There’s a time when, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption …

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: third absorption …

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati,
segs.e: fourth absorption.

segs.p: tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhussa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: At that time the mendicant thinks,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dānāhaṁ etarahi attanā viharāmi akaraṇīyo mārassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now I’m in a secure location and Māra can’t do anything to me.’

segs.p: Mārassāpi, bhikkhave, pāpimato evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And Māra the Wicked also thinks,

segs.p: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni bhikkhu etarahi attanā viharati, akaraṇīyo mayhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now the mendicant is in a secure location and we can’t do anything to them.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: There’s a time when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu antamakāsi māraṁ, apadaṁ vadhitvā māracakkhuṁ adassanaṁ gato pāpimato tiṇṇo loke visattikan’ti.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra, put out his eyes without a trace, and gone where the Wicked One cannot see.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: There’s a time when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …

segs.p: sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness. …

segs.p: sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. …

segs.p: sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu antamakāsi māraṁ, apadaṁ vadhitvā māracakkhuṁ adassanaṁ gato pāpimato tiṇṇo loke visattikan’”ti.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra, put out his eyes without a trace, and gone where the Wicked One cannot see. And they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.40
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.40

segs.p: 4. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 4. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Nāgasutta
segs.e: The Simile of the Bull Elephant in the Forest

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa gocarapasutassa hatthīpi hatthiniyopi hatthikalabhāpi hatthicchāpāpi purato purato gantvā tiṇaggāni chindanti, tena, bhikkhave, āraññiko nāgo aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a wild bull elephant is engrossed in the pasture, but other elephants—males, females, younglings, or cubs—got there first and trampled the grass, the wild bull elephant is horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa gocarapasutassa hatthīpi hatthiniyopi hatthikalabhāpi hatthicchāpāpi obhaggobhaggaṁ sākhābhaṅgaṁ khādanti, tena, bhikkhave, āraññiko nāgo aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati.
segs.e: When the wild bull elephant is engrossed in the pasture, but other elephants—males, females, younglings, or cubs—eat the broken branches that he has dragged down, the wild bull elephant is horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa ogāhaṁ otiṇṇassa hatthīpi hatthiniyopi hatthikalabhāpi hatthicchāpāpi purato purato gantvā soṇḍāya udakaṁ āloḷenti, tena, bhikkhave, āraññiko nāgo aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati.
segs.e: When a wild bull elephant has plunged into the pool, but other elephants—males, females, younglings, or cubs—got there first and stirred up the water with their trunks, the wild bull elephant is horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa ogāhā uttiṇṇassa hatthiniyo kāyaṁ upanighaṁsantiyo gacchanti, tena, bhikkhave, āraññiko nāgo aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati.
segs.e: When a wild bull elephant has come out of the pool and the female elephants bump into him, the wild bull elephant is horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: At that time the wild bull elephant thinks:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho etarahi ākiṇṇo viharāmi hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikalabhehi hatthicchāpehi.
segs.e: ‘These days I live crowded by other males, females, younglings, and cubs.

segs.p: Chinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādāmi, obhaggobhaggañca me sākhābhaṅgaṁ khādanti, āvilāni ca pānīyāni pivāmi, ogāhā ca me uttiṇṇassa hatthiniyo kāyaṁ upanighaṁsantiyo gacchanti.
segs.e: I eat the grass they’ve trampled, and they eat the broken branches I’ve dragged down. I drink muddy water, and after my bath the female elephants bump into me.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I live alone, withdrawn from the herd?’

segs.p: So aparena samayena eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho viharati, acchinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādati, obhaggobhaggañcassa sākhābhaṅgaṁ na khādanti, anāvilāni ca pānīyāni pivati, ogāhā cassa uttiṇṇassa na hatthiniyo kāyaṁ upanighaṁsantiyo gacchanti.
segs.e: After some time he lives alone, withdrawn from the herd, and he eats untrampled grass, and other elephants don’t eat the broken branches he has dragged down. He doesn’t drink muddy water, and the female elephants don’t bump into him after his bath.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye āraññikassa nāgassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: At that time the wild bull elephant thinks:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho pubbe ākiṇṇo vihāsiṁ hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikalabhehi hatthicchāpehi, chinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādiṁ, obhaggobhaggañca me sākhābhaṅgaṁ khādiṁsu, āvilāni ca pānīyāni apāyiṁ, ogāhā ca me uttiṇṇassa hatthiniyo kāyaṁ upanighaṁsantiyo agamaṁsu. Sohaṁ etarahi eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho viharāmi, acchinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādāmi, obhaggobhaggañca me sākhābhaṅgaṁ na khādanti, anāvilāni ca pānīyāni pivāmi, ogāhā ca me uttiṇṇassa na hatthiniyo kāyaṁ upanighaṁsantiyo gacchantī’ti. So soṇḍāya sākhābhaṅgaṁ bhañjitvā sākhābhaṅgena kāyaṁ parimajjitvā attamano soṇḍaṁ saṁharati.
segs.e: ‘Formerly I lived crowded by other males, females, younglings, and cubs. I ate the grass they’d trampled, and they ate the broken branches I’d dragged down. I drank muddy water, and after my bath the female elephants bumped into me. Now I live alone, and I’m free of all these things.’ He breaks off a branch and scratches his body, happily relieving his itches.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu ākiṇṇo viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi, tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhussa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant lives crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and by monastics of other religions and their disciples, they think:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho etarahi ākiṇṇo viharāmi bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
segs.e: ‘These days I live crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and monastics of other religions and their disciples.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I live alone, withdrawn from the group?’

segs.p: So vivittaṁ senāsanaṁ bhajati araññaṁ rukkhamūlaṁ pabbataṁ kandaraṁ giriguhaṁ susānaṁ vanapatthaṁ abbhokāsaṁ palālapuñjaṁ.
segs.e: They frequent a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

segs.p: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, they sit down cross-legged, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present.

segs.p: So abhijjhaṁ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up covetousness for the world, they meditate with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

segs.p: byāpādapadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up ill will and malevolence, they meditate with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

segs.p: thinamiddhaṁ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, they meditate with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

segs.p: uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up restlessness and remorse, they meditate without restlessness, their mind settled internally, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

segs.p: vicikicchaṁ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṅkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up doubt, they meditate having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

segs.p: So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe
segs.e: They give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

segs.p: vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: So attamano soṇḍaṁ saṁharati.
segs.e: They happily relieve their itches.

segs.p: Vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption …

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: third absorption …

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: fourth absorption.

segs.p: So attamano soṇḍaṁ saṁharati.
segs.e: They happily relieve their itches.

segs.p: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: So attamano soṇḍaṁ saṁharati.
segs.e: They happily relieve their itches.

segs.p: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …

segs.p: sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness. …

segs.p: sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. …

segs.p: sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

segs.p: So attamano soṇḍaṁ saṁharatī”ti.
segs.e: They happily relieve their itches.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.41
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.41

segs.p: 4. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 4. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Tapussasutta
segs.e: With the Householder Tapussa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu viharati uruvelakappaṁ nāma mallānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Mallas, near the Mallian town named Uruvelakappa.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya uruvelakappaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Uruvelakappa for alms.

segs.p: Uruvelakappe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, after the meal, on his return from almsround, he addressed Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “idheva tāva tvaṁ, ānanda, hohi, yāvāhaṁ mahāvanaṁ ajjhogāhāmi divāvihārāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Ānanda, you stay right here, while I plunge deep into the Great Wood for the day’s meditation.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā mahāvanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha plunged deep into the Great Wood and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho tapusso gahapati yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho tapusso gahapati āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The householder Tapussa went up to Venerable Ānanda, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Mayaṁ, bhante ānanda, gihī kāmabhogino kāmārāmā kāmaratā kāmasammuditā.
segs.e: “Honorable Ānanda, we are laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures. We like sensual pleasures, we love them and take joy in them.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ gihīnaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ kāmārāmānaṁ kāmaratānaṁ kāmasammuditānaṁ papāto viya khāyati, yadidaṁ nekkhammaṁ.
segs.e: But renunciation seems like an abyss.

segs.p: Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, ‘imasmiṁ dhammavinaye daharānaṁ daharānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: I have heard that in this teaching and training there are very young mendicants whose minds leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in renunciation. They see it as peaceful.

segs.p: Tayidaṁ, bhante, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye bhikkhūnaṁ bahunā janena visabhāgo, yadidaṁ nekkhamman”ti.
segs.e: Renunciation is the dividing line between the multitude and the mendicants in this teaching and training.”

segs.p: “Atthi kho etaṁ, gahapati, kathāpābhataṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: “Householder, we should see the Buddha about this matter.

segs.p: Āyāma, gahapati, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocessāma.
segs.e: Come, let’s go to the Buddha and inform him about this.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā”ti.
segs.e: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho tapusso gahapati āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Tapussa.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando tapussena gahapatinā saddhiṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda together with Tapussa went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Ānanda told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Ayaṁ, bhante, tapusso gahapati evamāha:

‘mayaṁ, bhante ānanda, gihī kāmabhogino kāmārāmā kāmaratā kāmasammuditā, tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ gihīnaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ kāmārāmānaṁ kāmaratānaṁ kāmasammuditānaṁ papāto viya khāyati, yadidaṁ nekkhammaṁ’.
Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, ‘imasmiṁ dhammavinaye daharānaṁ daharānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
Tayidaṁ, bhante, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye bhikkhūnaṁ bahunā janena visabhāgo yadidaṁ nekkhamman’”ti.
“Evametaṁ, ānanda, evametaṁ, ānanda.
segs.e: “That’s so true, Ānanda! That’s so true!

segs.p: Mayhampi kho, ānanda, pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: Before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I too thought,

segs.p: ‘sādhu nekkhammaṁ, sādhu paviveko’ti.
segs.e: ‘Renunciation is good! Seclusion is good!’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nekkhamme cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in renunciation. I didn’t see it as peaceful.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo, yena me nekkhamme cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
segs.e: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in renunciation? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘kāmesu kho me ādīnavo adiṭṭho, so ca me abahulīkato, nekkhamme ca ānisaṁso anadhigato, so ca me anāsevito.
segs.e: ‘I haven’t seen the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, and so I haven’t cultivated that. I haven’t realized the benefits of renunciation, and so I haven’t developed that.

segs.p: Tasmā me nekkhamme cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: That’s why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in renunciation. And it’s why I don’t see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘sace kho ahaṁ kāmesu ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, nekkhamme ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ,
segs.e: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of renunciation, I were to develop that.

segs.p: ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in renunciation. And I would see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena kāmesu ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, nekkhamme ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of sensual pleasures and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of renunciation and developed that.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: Then my mind leapt forth, gained confidence, settled down, and became decided in renunciation. I saw it as peaceful.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I entered and remained in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, iminā vihārena viharato kāmasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by sensual pleasures beset me, and that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sukhino dukkhaṁ uppajjeyya yāvadeva ābādhāya;
segs.e: Suppose a happy person were to experience pain; that would be an affliction for them.

segs.p: evamevassa me kāmasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: In the same way, when perception and focus accompanied by sensual pleasures beset me, that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘yannūnāhaṁ vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Why don’t I, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … enter and remain in the second absorption?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, avitakke cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in not placing the mind. I didn’t see it as peaceful.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo, yena me avitakke cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
segs.e: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in not placing the mind? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘sace kho ahaṁ viññāṇañcāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, ākiñcaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me ākiñcaññāyatane cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of the dimension of infinite consciousness, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of the dimension of nothingness, I were to develop that. It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of nothingness. And I would see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena viññāṇañcāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, ākiñcaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of the dimension of infinite consciousness and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of the dimension of nothingness and developed that.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, ākiñcaññāyatane cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: Then my mind leapt forth, gained confidence, settled down, and became decided in the dimension of nothingness. I saw it as peaceful.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, I entered and remained in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, iminā vihārena viharato viññāṇañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of infinite consciousness beset me, and that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sukhino dukkhaṁ uppajjeyya yāvadeva ābādhāya;
segs.e: Suppose a happy person were to experience pain; that would be an affliction for them.

segs.p: evamevassa me viññāṇañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: In the same way, when perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of infinite consciousness beset me, that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘yannūnāhaṁ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Why don’t I, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. I didn’t see it as peaceful.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo, yena me nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
segs.e: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘ākiñcaññāyatane kho me ādīnavo adiṭṭho, so ca me abahulīkato, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ca ānisaṁso anadhigato, so ca me anāsevito.
segs.e: ‘I haven’t seen the drawbacks of the dimension of nothingness, and so I haven’t cultivated that. I haven’t realized the benefits of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and so I haven’t developed that.

segs.p: Tasmā me nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: That’s why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And it’s why I don’t see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘sace kho ahaṁ ākiñcaññāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of the dimension of nothingness, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, I were to develop that. It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And I would see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena ākiñcaññāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of the dimension of nothingness and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception and developed that.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: Then my mind leapt forth, gained confidence, settled down, and became decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. I saw it as peaceful.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, I entered and remained in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, iminā vihārena viharato ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of nothingness beset me, and that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sukhino dukkhaṁ uppajjeyya yāvadeva ābādhāya;
segs.e: Suppose a happy person were to experience pain; that would be an affliction for them.

segs.p: evamevassa me ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa me hoti ābādho.
segs.e: In the same way, when perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of nothingness beset me, that was an affliction for me.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘yannūnāhaṁ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Why don’t I, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, saññāvedayitanirodhe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the cessation of perception and feeling. I didn’t see it as peaceful.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho hetu, ko paccayo, yena me saññāvedayitanirodhe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
segs.e: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the cessation of perception and feeling? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘nevasaññānāsaññāyatane kho me ādīnavo adiṭṭho, so ca me abahulīkato, saññāvedayitanirodhe ca ānisaṁso anadhigato, so ca me anāsevito.
segs.e: ‘I haven’t seen the drawbacks of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and so I haven’t cultivated that. I haven’t realized the benefits of the cessation of perception and feeling, and so I haven’t developed that.

segs.p: Tasmā me saññāvedayitanirodhe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: That’s why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the cessation of perception and feeling. And it’s why I don’t see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
segs.e: Then I thought,

segs.p: ‘sace kho ahaṁ nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, saññāvedayitanirodhe ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me saññāvedayitanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
segs.e: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of the cessation of perception and feeling, I were to develop that. It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the cessation of perception and feeling. And I would see it as peaceful.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, saññāvedayitanirodhe ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of the cessation of perception and feeling and developed that.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, saññāvedayitanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
segs.e: Then my mind did leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the cessation of perception and feeling. I saw it as peaceful.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharāmi, paññāya ca me disvā āsavā parikkhayaṁ agamaṁsu.
segs.e: And so, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, I entered and remained in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, my defilements were ended.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, ānanda, imā nava anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo na evaṁ anulomapaṭilomaṁ samāpajjimpi vuṭṭhahimpi, neva tāvāhaṁ, ānanda, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: As long as I hadn’t entered into and withdrawn from these nine progressive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: Yato ca kho ahaṁ, ānanda, imā nava anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo evaṁ anulomapaṭilomaṁ samāpajjimpi vuṭṭhahimpi, athāhaṁ, ānanda, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: But when I had entered into and withdrawn from these nine progressive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṁ udapādi:
segs.e: Knowledge and vision arose in me:

segs.p: ‘akuppā me cetovimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Mahāvaggo catuttho.
Tassuddānaṁ
Dve vihārā ca nibbānaṁ,
gāvī jhānena pañcamaṁ;
Ānando brāhmaṇā devo,
nāgena tapussena cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.42
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.42

segs.p: 5. Sāmaññavagga
segs.e: 5. Similarity

segs.p: Sambādhasutta
segs.e: Cramped

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Udāyī went up to Venerable Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā udāyī āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Ānanda,

segs.p: “vuttamidaṁ, āvuso, pañcālacaṇḍena devaputtena:
segs.e: “Reverend, this was said by the godling Pañcālacaṇḍa:

segs.p: ‘Sambādhe gataṁ okāsaṁ,
segs.e: ‘The opening amid confinement

segs.p: Avidvā bhūrimedhaso;
segs.e: was discovered by the Buddha of vast intelligence,

segs.p: Yo jhānamabujjhi buddho,
segs.e: who awakened to absorption,

segs.p: Paṭilīnanisabho munī’ti.
segs.e: the sage, the solitary boss bull.’

segs.p: Katamo, āvuso, sambādho, katamo sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: But what is confinement, and what is the opening amid confinement that the Buddha spoke of?”

segs.p: “Pañcime, āvuso, kāmaguṇā sambādho vutto bhagavatā.
segs.e: “Reverend, these five kinds of sensual stimulation are called ‘confinement’ by the Buddha.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
segs.e: Sights known by the eye that are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: sotaviññeyyā saddā …pe…
segs.e: Sounds known by the ear …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: Smells known by the nose …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: Tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, pañca kāmaguṇā sambādho vutto bhagavatā.
segs.e: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation that are called ‘confinement’ by the Buddha.

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Now, take a mendicant who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … enters and remains in the first absorption.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha vitakkavicārā aniruddhā honti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever placing of the mind and keeping it connected has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … enters and remains in the second absorption.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha pīti aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever rapture has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, with the fading away of rapture … enters and remains in the third absorption.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of creating an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha upekkhāsukhaṁ aniruddhaṁ hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever bliss with equanimity has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, giving up pleasure and pain … enters and remains in the fourth absorption.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha rūpasaññā aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever perception of form has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever perception of the dimension of infinite space has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever perception of the dimension of nothingness has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Tatrāpatthi sambādho.
segs.e: But it is still confined.

segs.p: Kiñca tattha sambādho?
segs.e: Confined by what?

segs.p: Yadeva tattha nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā aniruddhā hoti, ayamettha sambādho.
segs.e: Whatever perception of neither perception nor non-perception has not ceased is the confinement there.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, sambādhe okāsādhigamo vutto bhagavatā nippariyāyenā”ti.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of an opening amid confinement in a definitive sense.”

segs.p: Kāyasakkhīsutta
segs.e: A Direct Witness

segs.p: “‘Kāyasakkhī, kāyasakkhī’ti, āvuso, vuccati.
segs.e: “Reverend, they speak of the ‘direct witness’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, kāyasakkhī vutto bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: What is the direct witness that the Buddha spoke of?”

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “First, take a mendicant who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … enters and remains in the first absorption.

segs.p: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, kāyasakkhī vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the direct witness in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption …

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: third absorption …

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: fourth absorption.

segs.p: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, kāyasakkhī vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the direct witness in a qualified sense.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, kāyasakkhī vutto bhagavatā pariyāyena …pe….
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the direct witness in a qualified sense. Furthermore, take a mendicant who enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness … the dimension of nothingness … the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

segs.p: Yathā yathā ca tadāyatanaṁ tathā tathā naṁ kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate directly experiencing that dimension in every way.

segs.p: Ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, kāyasakkhī vutto bhagavatā nippariyāyenā”ti.
segs.e: To this extent the Buddha spoke of the direct witness in a definitive sense.”

segs.p: Abhabbasutta
segs.e: Impossible

segs.p: “Nava, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up nine things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Rāgaṁ, dosaṁ, mohaṁ, kodhaṁ, upanāhaṁ, makkhaṁ, paḷāsaṁ, issaṁ, macchariyaṁ—
segs.e: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, and stinginess.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, nava dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these nine things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Nava, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up nine things you can realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Rāgaṁ, dosaṁ, mohaṁ, kodhaṁ, upanāhaṁ, makkhaṁ, paḷāsaṁ, issaṁ, macchariyaṁ—
segs.e: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, and stinginess.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, nava dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these nine things you can realize the fruit of perfection.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Khemavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Khemo ca amatañceva,
Abhayaṁ passaddhiyena ca;
Nirodho anupubbo ca,
Dhammaṁ pahāya bhabbena cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.63
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.63

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Sikkhādubbalyasutta
segs.e: Weaknesses in Training and Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṁ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ—
segs.e: Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: These are the five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: vedanāsu …pe…
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

segs.p: citte …
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …

segs.p: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up those five weaknesses in your training you should develop these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.64
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.64

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Nīvaraṇasutta
segs.e: Hindrances

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five hindrances.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṁ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṁ, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṁ, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṁ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṁ—
segs.e: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇāni.
segs.e: These are the five hindrances.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ nīvaraṇānaṁ pahānāya cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five hindrances you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: vedanāsu …pe…
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

segs.p: citte …
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …

segs.p: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ nīvaraṇānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up those five hindrances you should develop these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.65
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.65
