segs.p: Kāmaguṇasutta
segs.e: Kinds of Sensual Stimulation

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
segs.e: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: sotaviññeyyā saddā …pe…
segs.e: Sounds known by the ear …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: Smells known by the nose …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: Tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā.
segs.e: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five kinds of sensual stimulation you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.66
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.66

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Upādānakkhandhasutta
segs.e: Grasping Aggregates

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, upādānakkhandhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho—
segs.e: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā.
segs.e: These are the five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five grasping aggregates you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.67
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.67

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Orambhāgiyasutta
segs.e: Lower Fetters

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are five lower fetters.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, kāmacchando, byāpādo—
segs.e: Substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, sensual desire, and ill will.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcorambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni.
segs.e: These are the five lower fetters.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five lower fetters you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.68
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.68

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Gatisutta
segs.e: Places of Rebirth

segs.p: “Pañcimā, bhikkhave, gatiyo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are five destinations.

segs.p: Katamā pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Nirayo, tiracchānayoni, pettivisayo, manussā, devā—
segs.e: Hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, humanity, and the gods.

segs.p: imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca gatiyo.
segs.e: These are the five destinations.

segs.p: Imāsaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ gatīnaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five destinations you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.69
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.69

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Macchariyasutta
segs.e: Stinginess

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, macchariyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five kinds of stinginess.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Āvāsamacchariyaṁ, kulamacchariyaṁ, lābhamacchariyaṁ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṁ, dhammamacchariyaṁ—
segs.e: Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teaching.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca macchariyāni.
segs.e: These are the five kinds of stinginess.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ macchariyānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five kinds of stinginess you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.70
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.70

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Uddhambhāgiyasutta
segs.e: Higher Fetters

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are five higher fetters.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṁ, avijjā—
segs.e: Desire for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, desire for rebirth in the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni.
segs.e: These are the five higher fetters.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ uddhambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five higher fetters you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.71
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.71

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Cetokhilasutta
segs.e: Hard-heartedness

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, cetokhilā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are five kinds of hard-heartedness.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetokhilo.
segs.e: This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …

segs.p: saṅghe kaṅkhati …
segs.e: the Saṅgha …

segs.p: sikkhāya kaṅkhati …
segs.e: the training …

segs.p: sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto.
segs.e: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetokhilo.
segs.e: This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetokhilānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five kinds of hard-heartedness you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.72
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.72

segs.p: 7. Satipaṭṭhānavagga
segs.e: 7. Mindfulness Meditation

segs.p: Cetasovinibandhasutta
segs.e: Shackles of the Heart

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, cetasovinibandhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five shackles of the heart.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho.
segs.e: This is the first shackle of the heart.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant isn’t free of greed for the body …

segs.p: rūpe avītarāgo hoti …
segs.e: They’re not free of greed for form …

segs.p: yāvadatthaṁ udarāvadehakaṁ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharati …
segs.e: They eat as much as they like until their belly is full, then indulge in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing …

segs.p: aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti.
segs.e: They lead the spiritual life wishing to be reborn in one of the orders of gods: ‘By this precept or observance or fervent austerity or spiritual practice, may I become one of the gods!’

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetasovinibandho.
segs.e: This is the fifth shackle of the heart.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca cetasovinibandhā.
segs.e: These are the five shackles of the heart.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetasovinibandhānaṁ pahānāya cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five shackles of the heart you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: vedanāsu …pe…
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

segs.p: citte …
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …

segs.p: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetasovinibandhānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five shackles of the heart you should develop these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Satipaṭṭhānavaggo dutiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Sikkhā nīvaraṇākāmā,
Khandhā ca orambhāgiyā gati;
Maccheraṁ uddhambhāgiyā aṭṭhamaṁ,
Cetokhilā vinibandhāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.73
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.73

segs.p: 8. Sammappadhānavagga
segs.e: 8. Right Efforts

segs.p: Sikkhasutta
segs.e: Weaknesses in Training and Effort

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipāto …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ—
segs.e: Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: These are the five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop the four right efforts.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ anuppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

segs.p: uppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati;
segs.e: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

segs.p: anuppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ uppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati;
segs.e: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

segs.p: uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop these four right efforts.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.74–81
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.74–81

segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti …pe…
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures. …

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca cetasovinibandhā.
segs.e: These are the five shackles of the heart.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetasovinibandhānaṁ pahānāya cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five shackles of the heart you should develop the four right efforts.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ anuppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise. …

segs.p: uppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya …
segs.e: so that unskillful qualities are given up …

segs.p: anuppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ uppādāya …
segs.e: so that skillful qualities arise …

segs.p: uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetasovinibandhānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five shackles of the hearts you should develop these four right efforts.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Sammappadhānavaggo tatiyo.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.83
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.83

segs.p: 9. Iddhipādavagga
segs.e: 9. Bases of Psychic Power

segs.p: Sikkhasutta
segs.e: Weaknesses in Training and the Bases of Psychic Power

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipāto …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ—
segs.e: Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca sikkhādubbalyāni.
segs.e: These are the five weaknesses when you’re training.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya cattāro iddhipādā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop the four bases of psychic power.

segs.p: Katame cattāro?
segs.e: What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṁ iddhipādaṁ bhāveti,
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

segs.p: vīriyasamādhi …
segs.e: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort.

segs.p: cittasamādhi …
segs.e: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort.

segs.p: vīmaṁsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṁ iddhipādaṁ bhāveti.
segs.e: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ sikkhādubbalyānaṁ pahānāya ime cattāro iddhipādā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop these four bases of psychic power.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.84–91
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.84–91

segs.p: 10. Rāgapeyyāla
segs.e: 10. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (1st)

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya nava dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For insight into greed, nine things should be developed.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of ugliness, death, repulsiveness of food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, impermanence, suffering in impermanence, not-self in suffering, giving up, and fading away.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime nava dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these nine things should be developed.”

segs.p: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 9.94

segs.p: 10. Rāgapeyyāla
segs.e: 10. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (2nd)

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya nava dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For insight into greed, nine things should be developed.

segs.p: Katame nava?
segs.e: What nine?

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ, dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ, tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ, catutthaṁ jhānaṁ, ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ, viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ, ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ, saññāvedayitanirodho—
segs.e: The first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption, the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness, the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and the cessation of perception and feeling.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime nava dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these nine things should be developed.”
